# Fluid Framework Documentation | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs

## What is Fluid Framework?[](https://fluidframework.com#what-is-fluid-framework)

Fluid Framework is a collection of client libraries for distributing and synchronizing shared state. These libraries allow multiple clients to simultaneously create and operate on shared data structures using coding patterns similar to those used to work with local data.

## Why Fluid?[](https://fluidframework.com#why-fluid)

Because building low-latency, collaborative experiences is hard!

Fluid Framework offers:

- Client-centric application model with data persistence requiring no custom server code.
- Distributed data structures with familiar programming patterns.
- Very low latency.

The developers at Microsoft have built collaboration into many applications, but many required application specific server-side logic to manage the collaborative experience. The Fluid Framework is the result of Microsoft's investment in reducing the complexity of creating collaborative applications.

What if you didn't have to invest in server code at all? Imagine if you could use a general purpose server which was designed to be lightweight and low cost. Imagine if all your development was focused on the client experience and data sync was handled for you. That is the promise of Fluid.

## Focused on the client developer[](https://fluidframework.com#focused-on-the-client-developer)

Applications built with Fluid Framework require zero custom code on the server to enable sophisticated data sync scenarios such as real-time typing across text editors. Client developers can focus on customer experiences while letting Fluid do the work of keeping data in sync.

Fluid Framework works with your application framework of choice.
Whether you prefer plain JavaScript or a framework like [React](https://react.dev), [Angular](https://angular.io),
or [Vue](https://vuejs.org), Fluid Framework makes building collaborative experiences simple and flexible.

## How Fluid works[](https://fluidframework.com#how-fluid-works)

Fluid was designed to deliver collaborative experiences with blazing performance. To achieve this goal, the team kept the server logic as simple and lightweight as possible. This approach helped ensure virtually instant syncing across clients with very low server costs.

To keep the server simple, each Fluid client is responsible for its own state. While previous systems keep a source of truth on the server, the Fluid service is responsible for taking in data operations, sequencing the operations, and returning the sequenced operations to the clients. Each client is able to use that sequence to independently and accurately produce the current state regardless of the order it receives operations.

The following is a typical flow.

- Client code changes data locally.
- Fluid runtime sends that change to the Fluid service.
- Fluid service sequences that operation and broadcasts it to all clients.
- Fluid runtime incorporates that operation into local data and raises a "valueChanged" event.
- Client code handles that event (updates view, runs business logic).

## Next steps[](https://fluidframework.com#next-steps)

If you want to learn a lot more about how Fluid works, start with our
** architecture** overview.

If you prefer to get your hands dirty right away, head for our coding ** tutorial** and

**. But first, get your**

[examples](https://fluidframework.com/docs/start/examples)**set up.**

# Fluid Framework API Overview | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/

To get started with the Fluid Framework, you'll want to take a dependency on our client library, [fluid-framework](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-framework).

You'll then want to pair that with the appropriate service client implementation based on your service. These include:

- [@fluidframework/azure-client](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/)(for use with- [Azure Fluid Relay](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/deployment/azure-fluid-relay))
- [@fluidframework/tinylicious-client](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/tinylicious-client/)(for testing with- [Tinylicious](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/testing/tinylicious))

For more information on our service client implementations, see [Fluid Services](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/deployment/service-options).

---

# @fluidframework/aqueduct Package | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/

The `aqueduct` package is a library for building Fluid objects and Fluid containers within the Fluid Framework. Its goal is to provide a thin base layer over the existing Fluid Framework interfaces that allows developers to get started quickly.

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#_fluidframework_aqueduct-remarks)

About the package name: An Aqueduct is a way to transport water from a source to another location. The package name was chosen because its purpose is to facilitate using lower level constructs and therefore handle 'fluid' items same as an aqueduct.

## Interfaces[](https://fluidframework.com#interfaces)

| Interface | Description |
|---|---|
| [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | This type is used as the base generic input to DataObject and PureDataObject. |
| [IDataObjectProps](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/idataobjectprops-interface) | |
| [IRootDataObjectFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/irootdataobjectfactory-interface) |

## Classes[](https://fluidframework.com#classes)

| Class | Description |
|---|---|
| [BaseContainerRuntimeFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class) | BaseContainerRuntimeFactory produces container runtimes with a given data store and service registry, as well as given request handlers. It can be subclassed to implement a first-time initialization procedure for the containers it creates. |
| [BaseContainerService](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerservice-class) | This class is a simple starter class for building a Container Service. It simply provides routing |
| [ContainerRuntimeFactoryWithDefaultDataStore](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/containerruntimefactorywithdefaultdatastore-class) | A ContainerRuntimeFactory that initializes Containers with a single default data store, which can be requested from the container with an empty URL. This factory should be exposed as fluidExport off the entry point to your module. |
| [DataObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class) | DataObject is a base data store that is primed with a root directory. It ensures that it is created and ready before you can access it. Having a single root directory allows for easier development. Instead of creating and registering channels with the runtime any new DDS that is set on the root will automatically be registered. |
| [DataObjectFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjectfactory-class) | DataObjectFactory is the IFluidDataStoreFactory for use with DataObjects. It facilitates DataObject's features (such as its shared directory) by ensuring relevant shared objects etc are available to the factory. |
| [PureDataObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobject-class) | This is a bare-bones base class that does basic setup and enables for factory on an initialize call. You probably don't want to inherit from this data store directly unless you are creating another base data store class |
| [PureDataObjectFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class) | PureDataObjectFactory is a barebones IFluidDataStoreFactory for use with PureDataObject. Consumers should typically use DataObjectFactory instead unless creating another base data store factory. |

Mounting across bundle boundaries breaks some frameworks, so the mountable view is used to ensure the mounting is done within the same bundle as the view. For example, React hooks don't work if mounted across bundles since there will be two React instances, breaking the Rules of Hooks. When cross-bundle mounting isn't required, the mountable view isn't necessary. When a request is received with a mountableView: true header, this request handler will reissue the request without the header, and respond with a mountable view of the given class using the response. |
| [serviceRoutePathRoot](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/#serviceroutepathroot-variable) |

## Function Details[](https://fluidframework.com#function-details)

### defaultFluidObjectRequestHandler[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultfluidobjectrequesthandler-function)

Default request handler for a Fluid object that returns the object itself if: 1. the request url is empty 2. the request url is "/" 3. the request url starts with "/" and is followed by a query param, such as /?key=value Returns a 404 error for any other url.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultfluidobjectrequesthandler-signature)

```
export declare function defaultFluidObjectRequestHandler(fluidObject: FluidObject, request: IRequest): IResponse;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultfluidobjectrequesthandler-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| fluidObject | [FluidObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/fluidobject-typealias) | |
| request | [IRequest](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/irequest-interface) |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultfluidobjectrequesthandler-returns)

**Return type**: [IResponse](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iresponse-interface)

### getDefaultObjectFromContainer[](https://fluidframework.com#getdefaultobjectfromcontainer-function)

Helper function for getting the default Fluid Object from a Container. This function only works for Containers that support "/" request.

T - defines the type you expect to be returned

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getdefaultobjectfromcontainer-signature)

```
export declare function getDefaultObjectFromContainer<T = FluidObject>(container: IContainer): Promise<T>;
```
##### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | [FluidObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/fluidobject-typealias) |

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#getdefaultobjectfromcontainer-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| container | [IContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface) | Container you're attempting to get the object from |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getdefaultobjectfromcontainer-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<T>

### getObjectFromContainer[](https://fluidframework.com#getobjectfromcontainer-function)

## Variable Details[](https://fluidframework.com#variable-details)

### defaultRouteRequestHandler[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultrouterequesthandler-variable)

Pipe through container request into internal request. If request is empty and default url is provided, redirect request to such default url.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#defaultrouterequesthandler-signature)

```
defaultRouteRequestHandler: (defaultRootId: string) => (request: IRequest, runtime: IContainerRuntime) => Promise<IResponse | undefined>
```
**Type**: (defaultRootId: string) => (request: [IRequest](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/irequest-interface), runtime: [IContainerRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime-definitions/icontainerruntime-interface)) => Promise<[IResponse](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iresponse-interface) | undefined>

### generateContainerServicesRequestHandler[](https://fluidframework.com#generatecontainerservicesrequesthandler-variable)

Given a collection of IContainerServices will produce a RequestHandler for them all

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#generatecontainerservicesrequesthandler-signature)

```
generateContainerServicesRequestHandler: (serviceRegistry: ContainerServiceRegistryEntries) => RuntimeRequestHandler
```
**Type**: (serviceRegistry: [ContainerServiceRegistryEntries](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/containerserviceregistryentries-typealias)) => [RuntimeRequestHandler](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/request-handler/runtimerequesthandler-typealias)

### mountableViewRequestHandler[](https://fluidframework.com#mountableviewrequesthandler-variable)

A mountable view is only required if the view needs to be mounted across a bundle boundary. Mounting across bundle boundaries breaks some frameworks, so the mountable view is used to ensure the mounting is done within the same bundle as the view. For example, React hooks don't work if mounted across bundles since there will be two React instances, breaking the Rules of Hooks. When cross-bundle mounting isn't required, the mountable view isn't necessary.

When a request is received with a mountableView: true header, this request handler will reissue the request without the header, and respond with a mountable view of the given class using the response.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#mountableviewrequesthandler-signature)

```
mountableViewRequestHandler: (MountableViewClass: IFluidMountableViewClass, handlers: RuntimeRequestHandler[]) => (request: RequestParser, runtime: IContainerRuntime) => Promise<IResponse>
```
**Type**: (MountableViewClass: [IFluidMountableViewClass](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/view-interfaces/ifluidmountableviewclass-interface), handlers: [RuntimeRequestHandler](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/request-handler/runtimerequesthandler-typealias)[]) => (request: [RequestParser](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-utils/requestparser-class), runtime: [IContainerRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime-definitions/icontainerruntime-interface)) => Promise<[IResponse](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iresponse-interface)>

### serviceRoutePathRoot[](https://fluidframework.com#serviceroutepathroot-variable)

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#serviceroutepathroot-signature)

```
serviceRoutePathRoot = "_services"
```

# BaseContainerRuntimeFactory Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class

BaseContainerRuntimeFactory produces container runtimes with a given data store and service registry, as well as given request handlers. It can be subclassed to implement a first-time initialization procedure for the containers it creates.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#basecontainerruntimefactory-signature)

```
export declare class BaseContainerRuntimeFactory extends RuntimeFactoryHelper implements IProvideFluidDataStoreRegistry
```
**Extends**: [RuntimeFactoryHelper](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-utils/runtimefactoryhelper-class)

**Implements**: [IProvideFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/iprovidefluiddatastoreregistry-interface)

## Constructors[](https://fluidframework.com#constructors)

| Constructor | Description |
|---|---|
| [(constructor)(registryEntries, dependencyContainer, requestHandlers, runtimeOptions)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#_constructor_-constructor) | Constructs a new instance of the `BaseContainerRuntimeFactory`class |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [IFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#ifluiddatastoreregistry-property) | [IFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastoreregistry-interface) |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [containerHasInitialized(runtime)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#containerhasinitialized-method) | Promise<void> | Subclasses may override containerHasInitialized to perform any steps after the container has initialized. This likely includes loading any data stores that are expected to be there at the outset. |
| [containerInitializingFirstTime(runtime)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#containerinitializingfirsttime-method) | Promise<void> | Subclasses may override containerInitializingFirstTime to perform any setup steps at the time the container is created. This likely includes creating any initial data stores that are expected to be there at the outset. |
| [instantiateFirstTime(runtime)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#instantiatefirsttime-method) | Promise<void> | |
| [instantiateFromExisting(runtime)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#instantiatefromexisting-method) | Promise<void> | |
| [preInitialize(context, existing)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/basecontainerruntimefactory-class#preinitialize-method) | Promise< [ContainerRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/containerruntime-class)> |

constructor(registryEntries: NamedFluidDataStoreRegistryEntries, dependencyContainer?: IFluidDependencySynthesizer | undefined, requestHandlers?: RuntimeRequestHandler[], runtimeOptions?: IContainerRuntimeOptions | undefined);

| requestHandlers | optional | [RuntimeRequestHandler](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/request-handler/runtimerequesthandler-typealias)[] | Request handlers for containers produced |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### containerHasInitialized[](https://fluidframework.com#containerhasinitialized-method)

Subclasses may override containerHasInitialized to perform any steps after the container has initialized. This likely includes loading any data stores that are expected to be there at the outset.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#containerhasinitialized-signature)

```
protected containerHasInitialized(runtime: IContainerRuntime): Promise<void>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#containerhasinitialized-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| runtime | [IContainerRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime-definitions/icontainerruntime-interface) | The container runtime for the container being initialized |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#containerhasinitialized-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<void>

### containerInitializingFirstTime[](https://fluidframework.com#containerinitializingfirsttime-method)

Subclasses may override containerInitializingFirstTime to perform any setup steps at the time the container is created. This likely includes creating any initial data stores that are expected to be there at the outset.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#containerinitializingfirsttime-signature)

```
protected containerInitializingFirstTime(runtime: IContainerRuntime): Promise<void>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#containerinitializingfirsttime-parameters)

# ContainerRuntimeFactoryWithDefaultDataStore Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/containerruntimefactorywithdefaultdatastore-class

A ContainerRuntimeFactory that initializes Containers with a single default data store, which can be requested from the container with an empty URL.

# DataObject Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class

DataObject is a base data store that is primed with a root directory. It ensures that it is created and ready before you can access it.

Having a single root directory allows for easier development. Instead of creating and registering channels with the runtime any new DDS that is set on the root will automatically be registered.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#dataobject-signature)

```
export declare abstract class DataObject<I extends DataObjectTypes = DataObjectTypes> extends PureDataObject<I>
```
**Extends**: [PureDataObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobject-class)

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | The optional input types used to strongly type the data object |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [root](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class#root-property) | [ISharedDirectory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/map/ishareddirectory-interface) | The root directory will either be ready or will return an error. If an error is thrown the root has not been correctly created/set. |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [getUninitializedErrorString(item)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class#getuninitializederrorstring-method) | string | Generates an error string indicating an item is uninitialized. |
| [initializeInternal(existing)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class#initializeinternal-method) | Promise<void> | Initializes internal objects and calls initialization overrides. Caller is responsible for ensuring this is only invoked once. |
| [request(request)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobject-class#request-method) | Promise< [IResponse](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iresponse-interface)> | Return this object if someone requests it directly We will return this object in two scenarios: 1. the request url is a "/" 2. the request url is empty |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### root[](https://fluidframework.com#root-property)

The root directory will either be ready or will return an error. If an error is thrown the root has not been correctly created/set.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#root-signature)

```
protected get root(): ISharedDirectory;
```
**Type**: [ISharedDirectory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/map/ishareddirectory-interface)

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### getUninitializedErrorString[](https://fluidframework.com#getuninitializederrorstring-method)

Generates an error string indicating an item is uninitialized.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getuninitializederrorstring-signature)

```
protected getUninitializedErrorString(item: string): string;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#getuninitializederrorstring-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| item | string | The name of the item that was uninitialized. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getuninitializederrorstring-returns)

**Return type**: string

### initializeInternal[](https://fluidframework.com#initializeinternal-method)

Initializes internal objects and calls initialization overrides. Caller is responsible for ensuring this is only invoked once.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#initializeinternal-signature)

```
initializeInternal(existing: boolean): Promise<void>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#initializeinternal-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| existing | boolean |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#initializeinternal-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<void>

### request[](https://fluidframework.com#request-method)

Return this object if someone requests it directly We will return this object in two scenarios: 1. the request url is a "/" 2. the request url is empty

# DataObjectFactory Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjectfactory-class

DataObjectFactory is the IFluidDataStoreFactory for use with DataObjects. It facilitates DataObject's features (such as its shared directory) by ensuring relevant shared objects etc are available to the factory.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#dataobjectfactory-signature)

# DataObjectTypes Interface | Fluid Framework

# PureDataObject Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobject-class

This is a bare-bones base class that does basic setup and enables for factory on an initialize call. You probably don't want to inherit from this data store directly unless you are creating another base data store class

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#puredataobject-signature)

```
export declare abstract class PureDataObject<I extends DataObjectTypes = DataObjectTypes> extends EventForwarder<I["Events"] & IEvent> implements IFluidLoadable, IFluidRouter, IProvideFluidHandle
```
**Extends**: EventForwarder<I["Events"] & IEvent

**Implements**: [IFluidLoadable](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/ifluidloadable-interface), [IFluidRouter](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/ifluidrouter-interface), [IProvideFluidHandle](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iprovidefluidhandle-interface)

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| I | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | The optional input types used to strongly type the data object |

## Constructors[](https://fluidframework.com#constructors)

| Constructor | Description |
|---|---|
| [(constructor)(props)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobject-class#_constructor_-constructor) | Constructs a new instance of the `PureDataObject`class |

## Static Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#static-methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|

### providers[](https://fluidframework.com#providers-property)

Providers are FluidObject keyed objects that provide back a promise to the corresponding FluidObject or undefined. Providers injected/provided by the Container and/or HostingApplication

To define providers set FluidObject interfaces in the OptionalProviders generic type for your data store

### finishInitialization[](https://fluidframework.com#finishinitialization-method)

Call this API to ensure PureDataObject is fully initialized. Initialization happens on demand, only on as-needed bases. In most cases you should allow factory/object to decide when to finish initialization. But if you are supplying your own implementation of DataStoreRuntime factory and overriding some methods and need a fully initialized object, then you can call this API to ensure object is fully initialized.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#finishinitialization-signature)

```
finishInitialization(existing: boolean): Promise<void>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#finishinitialization-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| existing | boolean |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#finishinitialization-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<void>

# PureDataObjectFactory Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class

PureDataObjectFactory is a barebones IFluidDataStoreFactory for use with PureDataObject. Consumers should typically use DataObjectFactory instead unless creating another base data store factory.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#puredataobjectfactory-signature)

```
export declare class PureDataObjectFactory<TObj extends PureDataObject<I>, I extends DataObjectTypes = DataObjectTypes> implements IFluidDataStoreFactory, Partial<IProvideFluidDataStoreRegistry>, IRootDataObjectFactory
```
**Implements**: [IFluidDataStoreFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastorefactory-interface), Partial<[IProvideFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/iprovidefluiddatastoreregistry-interface)>, [IRootDataObjectFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/irootdataobjectfactory-interface)

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| TObj | [PureDataObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobject-class)<I> | DataObject (concrete type) | |
| I | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | [DataObjectTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/dataobjecttypes-interface) | The input types for the DataObject |

## Constructors[](https://fluidframework.com#constructors)

| Constructor | Description |
|---|---|
| [(constructor)(type, ctor, sharedObjects, optionalProviders, registryEntries, runtimeClass)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#_constructor_-constructor) | Constructs a new instance of the `PureDataObjectFactory`class |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [IFluidDataStoreFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#ifluiddatastorefactory-property) | this | |
| [IFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#ifluiddatastoreregistry-property) | [IFluidDataStoreRegistry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastoreregistry-interface)| undefined | |
| [registryEntry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#registryentry-property) | [NamedFluidDataStoreRegistryEntry](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/namedfluiddatastoreregistryentry-typealias) | Convenience helper to get the data store's/factory's data store registry entry. The return type hides the factory's generics, easing grouping of registry entries that differ only in this way into the same array. |
| [type](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#type-property) | string |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [createChildInstance(parentContext, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createchildinstance-method) | Promise<TObj> | Creates a new instance of the object. Uses parent context's registry to build package path to this factory. In other words, registry of context passed in has to contain this factory, with the name that matches this factory's type. It is intended to be used by data store objects that create sub-objects. |
| [createInstance(runtime, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createinstance-method) | Promise<TObj> | Creates a new instance of the object. Uses container's registry to find this factory. It's expected that only container owners would use this functionality, as only such developers have knowledge of entries in container registry. The name in this registry for such record should match type of this factory. |
| [createInstanceCore(context, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createinstancecore-method) | Promise<TObj> | |
| [createNonRootInstanceCore(containerRuntime, packagePath, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createnonrootinstancecore-method) | Promise<TObj> | |
| [createPeerInstance(peerContext, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createpeerinstance-method) | Promise<TObj> | Creates a new instance of the object. Uses peer context's registry and its package path to identify this factory. In other words, registry of context passed in has to have this factory. Intended to be used by data store objects that need to create peers (similar) instances of existing objects. |
| [createRootInstance(rootDataStoreId, runtime, initialState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#createrootinstance-method) | Promise<TObj> | Creates a new root instance of the object. Uses container's registry to find this factory. It's expected that only container owners would use this functionality, as only such developers have knowledge of entries in container registry. The name in this registry for such record should match type of this factory. |
| [instantiateDataStore(context, existing)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/aqueduct/puredataobjectfactory-class#instantiatedatastore-method) | Promise< [FluidDataStoreRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/datastore/fluiddatastoreruntime-class)> | This is where we do data store setup. |

```

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### createChildInstance[](https://fluidframework.com#createchildinstance-method)

Creates a new instance of the object. Uses parent context's registry to build package path to this factory. In other words, registry of context passed in has to contain this factory, with the name that matches this factory's type. It is intended to be used by data store objects that create sub-objects.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#createchildinstance-signature)

```
createChildInstance(parentContext: IFluidDataStoreContext, initialState?: I["InitialState"]): Promise<TObj>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createchildinstance-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| parentContext | [IFluidDataStoreContext](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastorecontext-interface) | ||
| initialState | optional | I["InitialState"] | The initial state to provide to the created data store. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createchildinstance-returns)

an object created by this factory. Data store and objects created are not attached to container. They get attached only when a handle to one of them is attached to already attached objects.

**Return type**: Promise<TObj>

### createInstance[](https://fluidframework.com#createinstance-method)

Creates a new instance of the object. Uses container's registry to find this factory. It's expected that only container owners would use this functionality, as only such developers have knowledge of entries in container registry. The name in this registry for such record should match type of this factory.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#createinstance-signature)

```
createInstance(runtime: IContainerRuntimeBase, initialState?: I["InitialState"]): Promise<TObj>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createinstance-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| runtime | [IContainerRuntimeBase](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/icontainerruntimebase-interface) | container runtime. It's registry is used to create an object. | |
| initialState | optional | I["InitialState"] | The initial state to provide to the created component. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createinstance-returns)

an object created by this factory. Data store and objects created are not attached to container. They get attached only when a handle to one of them is attached to already attached objects.

**Return type**: Promise<TObj>

| context | [IFluidDataStoreContextDetached](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastorecontextdetached-interface) | ||

### createNonRootInstanceCore[](https://fluidframework.com#createnonrootinstancecore-method)

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createnonrootinstancecore-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| containerRuntime | [IContainerRuntimeBase](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/icontainerruntimebase-interface) | ||
| packagePath | Readonly<string[]> | ||
| initialState | optional | I["InitialState"] |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createnonrootinstancecore-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<TObj>

### createPeerInstance[](https://fluidframework.com#createpeerinstance-method)

Creates a new instance of the object. Uses peer context's registry and its package path to identify this factory. In other words, registry of context passed in has to have this factory. Intended to be used by data store objects that need to create peers (similar) instances of existing objects.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#createpeerinstance-signature)

```
createPeerInstance(peerContext: IFluidDataStoreContext, initialState?: I["InitialState"]): Promise<TObj>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createpeerinstance-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| peerContext | [IFluidDataStoreContext](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastorecontext-interface) | ||
| initialState | optional | I["InitialState"] | The initial state to provide to the created component. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createpeerinstance-returns)

an object created by this factory. Data store and objects created are not attached to container. They get attached only when a handle to one of them is attached to already attached objects.

**Return type**: Promise<TObj>

### createRootInstance[](https://fluidframework.com#createrootinstance-method)

Creates a new root instance of the object. Uses container's registry to find this factory. It's expected that only container owners would use this functionality, as only such developers have knowledge of entries in container registry. The name in this registry for such record should match type of this factory.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#createrootinstance-signature)

```
createRootInstance(rootDataStoreId: string, runtime: IContainerRuntime, initialState?: I["InitialState"]): Promise<TObj>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createrootinstance-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| rootDataStoreId | string | ||
| runtime | [IContainerRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime-definitions/icontainerruntime-interface) | container runtime. It's registry is used to create an object. | |
| initialState | optional | I["InitialState"] | The initial state to provide to the created component. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createrootinstance-returns)

an object created by this factory. Data store and objects created are not attached to container. They get attached only when a handle to one of them is attached to already attached objects.

**Return type**: Promise<TObj>

### instantiateDataStore[](https://fluidframework.com#instantiatedatastore-method)

This is where we do data store setup.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#instantiatedatastore-signature)

```
instantiateDataStore(context: IFluidDataStoreContext, existing: boolean): Promise<FluidDataStoreRuntime>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#instantiatedatastore-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| context | [IFluidDataStoreContext](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/ifluiddatastorecontext-interface) | data store context used to load a data store runtime |
| existing | boolean |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#instantiatedatastore-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<[FluidDataStoreRuntime](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/datastore/fluiddatastoreruntime-class)>

# @fluidframework/azure-client Package | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/

| [AzureClientProps](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclientprops-interface) | Props for initializing a new AzureClient instance |
| [AzureConnectionConfig](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureconnectionconfig-interface) | Parameters for establishing a connection with the Azure Fluid Relay. |
| [AzureContainerServices](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface) | AzureContainerServices is returned by the AzureClient alongside a FluidContainer. It holds the functionality specifically tied to the Azure Fluid Relay, and how the data stored in the FluidContainer is persisted in the backend and consumed by users. Any functionality regarding how the data is handled within the FluidContainer itself, i.e. which data objects or DDSes to use, will not be included here but rather on the FluidContainer class itself. |
| [AzureContainerVersion](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerversion-interface) | Container version metadata. |
| [AzureGetVersionsOptions](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuregetversionsoptions-interface) | Options for "Get Container Versions" API. |
| [AzureLocalConnectionConfig](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurelocalconnectionconfig-interface) | Parameters for establishing a local connection with a local instance of the Azure Fluid Relay. |
| [AzureMember](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuremember-interface) | Since Azure provides user names for all of its members, we extend the *@fluidframework/protocol-definitions#IMember*interface to include this service-specific value. It will be returned for all audience members connected to Azure. |
| [AzureRemoteConnectionConfig](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureremoteconnectionconfig-interface) | Parameters for establishing a remote connection with the Azure Fluid Relay. |
| [AzureUser](/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureuser-interface) | Since Azure provides user names for all of its members, we extend the [IUser](/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/iuser-interface)interface to include this service-specific value. * |

# AzureClient Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclient-class

AzureClient provides the ability to have a Fluid object backed by the Azure Fluid Relay or, when running with local tenantId, have it be backed by a local Azure Fluid Relay instance.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#azureclient-signature)

```
export declare class AzureClient
```

|---|---|---|
| [copyContainer(id, containerSchema, version)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclient-class#copycontainer-method) | Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services:[AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }> | Creates new detached container out of specific version of another container. |
| [createContainer(containerSchema)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclient-class#createcontainer-method) | Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services:[AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }> | Creates a new detached container instance in the Azure Fluid Relay. |
| [getContainer(id, containerSchema)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclient-class#getcontainer-method) | Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services:[AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }> | Accesses the existing container given its unique ID in the Azure Fluid Relay. |
| [getContainerVersions(id, options)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureclient-class#getcontainerversions-method) | Promise< [AzureContainerVersion](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerversion-interface)[]> | Get the list of versions for specific container. |

### copyContainer[](https://fluidframework.com#copycontainer-method)

Creates new detached container out of specific version of another container.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#copycontainer-signature)

```
copyContainer(id: string, containerSchema: ContainerSchema, version?: AzureContainerVersion): Promise<{
        container: IFluidContainer;
        services: AzureContainerServices;
    }>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#copycontainer-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | string | Unique ID of the source container in Azure Fluid Relay. | |
| containerSchema | [ContainerSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/containerschema-interface) | Container schema used to access data objects in the container. | |
| version | optional | [AzureContainerVersion](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerversion-interface) | Unique version of the source container in Azure Fluid Relay. It defaults to latest version if parameter not provided. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#copycontainer-returns)

New detached container instance along with associated services.

**Return type**: Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services: [AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }>

```
createContainer(containerSchema: ContainerSchema): Promise<{
        container: IFluidContainer;
        services: AzureContainerServices;
    }>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createcontainer-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| containerSchema | [ContainerSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/containerschema-interface) | Container schema for the new container. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createcontainer-returns)

New detached container instance along with associated services.

**Return type**: Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services: [AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }>

### getContainer[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainer-method)

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainer-signature)

```
getContainer(id: string, containerSchema: ContainerSchema): Promise<{
        container: IFluidContainer;
        services: AzureContainerServices;
    }>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainer-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| id | string | Unique ID of the container in Azure Fluid Relay. |
| containerSchema | [ContainerSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/containerschema-interface) | Container schema used to access data objects in the container. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainer-returns)

Existing container instance along with associated services.

**Return type**: Promise<{         container: [IFluidContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/ifluidcontainer-interface);         services: [AzureContainerServices](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface);     }>

### getContainerVersions[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainerversions-method)

Get the list of versions for specific container.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainerversions-signature)

```
getContainerVersions(id: string, options?: AzureGetVersionsOptions): Promise<AzureContainerVersion[]>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainerversions-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| id | string | Unique ID of the source container in Azure Fluid Relay. | |
| options | optional | [AzureGetVersionsOptions](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuregetversionsoptions-interface) | "Get" options. If options are not provided, API will assume maxCount of versions to retreive to be 5. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getcontainerversions-returns)

Array of available container versions.

**Return type**: Promise<[AzureContainerVersion](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerversion-interface)[]>

# AzureConnectionConfigType TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azureconnectionconfigtype-typealias

export declare type AzureConnectionConfigType = "local" | "remote";
```

# AzureContainerServices Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface

AzureContainerServices is returned by the AzureClient alongside a FluidContainer. It holds the functionality specifically tied to the Azure Fluid Relay, and how the data stored in the FluidContainer is persisted in the backend and consumed by users. Any functionality regarding how the data is handled within the FluidContainer itself, i.e. which data objects or DDSes to use, will not be included here but rather on the FluidContainer class itself.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#azurecontainerservices-signature)

```
export interface AzureContainerServices
```
## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [audience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azurecontainerservices-interface#audience-propertysignature) | [IAzureAudience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/iazureaudience-typealias) | Provides an object that can be used to get the users that are present in this Fluid session and listeners for when the roster has any changes from users joining/leaving the session |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### audience[](https://fluidframework.com#audience-propertysignature)

Provides an object that can be used to get the users that are present in this Fluid session and listeners for when the roster has any changes from users joining/leaving the session

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#audience-signature)

```
audience: IAzureAudience;
```
**Type**: [IAzureAudience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/iazureaudience-typealias)

---

# AzureMember Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuremember-interface

Since Azure provides user names for all of its members, we extend the *@fluidframework/protocol-definitions#IMember* interface to include this service-specific value. It will be returned for all audience members connected to Azure.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#azuremember-signature)

```
export interface AzureMember<T = any> extends IMember
```
**Extends**: [IMember](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/fluid-static/imember-interface)

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | any | See [additionalDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuremember-interface#additionaldetails-propertysignature). Note: must be JSON-serializable. Passing a non-serializable object (e.g. a`class`) will result in undefined behavior. |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [additionalDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuremember-interface#additionaldetails-propertysignature) | `optional` | T | Custom, app-specific user information |
| [userName](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-client/azuremember-interface#username-propertysignature) | string | The user's name |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### additionalDetails[](https://fluidframework.com#additionaldetails-propertysignature)

Custom, app-specific user information

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#additionaldetails-signature)

```
additionalDetails?: T;
```
**Type**: T

### userName[](https://fluidframework.com#username-propertysignature)

The user's name

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#username-signature)

```
userName: string;
```
**Type**: string

---

```
export interface AzureRemoteConnectionConfig extends AzureConnectionConfig

# @fluidframework/azure-service-utils Package | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-service-utils/

A set of helper utilities for building backend APIs for use with [Azure Fluid Relay](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/azure-fluid-relay/overview/overview).

Note that this library's primary entry-point ([generateToken(tenantId, key, scopes, documentId, user, lifetime, ver)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-service-utils/#generatetoken-function)) is only intended to be run in a browser context. It is **not** Node.js-compatible.

## Functions[](https://fluidframework.com#functions)

| Function | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [generateToken(tenantId, key, scopes, documentId, user, lifetime, ver)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/azure-service-utils/#generatetoken-function) | string | Generates a [JSON Web Token](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON_Web_Token)(JWT) to authorize access to a Routerlicious-based Fluid service. |

## Function Details[](https://fluidframework.com#function-details)

### generateToken[](https://fluidframework.com#generatetoken-function)

Generates a [JSON Web Token](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JSON_Web_Token) (JWT) to authorize access to a Routerlicious-based Fluid service.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#generatetoken-signature)

```
export declare function generateToken(tenantId: string, key: string, scopes: ScopeType[], documentId?: string, user?: IUser, lifetime?: number, ver?: string): string;
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#generatetoken-remarks)

Note: this function uses a browser friendly auth library ([jsrsasign](https://www.npmjs.com/package/jsrsasign)) and may only be used in client (browser) context. It is **not** Node.js-compatible.

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#generatetoken-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| tenantId | string | See [tenantId](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#tenantid-propertysignature) | |
| key | string | API key to authenticate user. Must be [UTF-8](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UTF-8)-encoded. | |
| scopes | [ScopeType](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/scopetype-enum)[] | See [scopes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#scopes-propertysignature) | |
| documentId | optional | string | See [documentId](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#documentid-propertysignature). If not specified, the token will not be associated with a document, and an empty string will be used. |
| user | optional | [IUser](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/iuser-interface) | User with whom generated tokens will be associated. If not specified, the token will not be associated with a user, and a randomly generated mock user will be used instead. See [user](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#user-propertysignature) |
| lifetime | optional | number | Used to generate the [expiration](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#exp-propertysignature). Expiration = now + lifetime. Expressed in seconds. Default: 3600 (1 hour). |
| ver | optional | string | See [ver](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/itokenclaims-interface#ver-propertysignature). Default:`1.0`. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#generatetoken-returns)

**Return type**: string

---

# SharedCell Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class

The SharedCell distributed data structure can be used to store a single serializable value.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#sharedcell-signature)

```
export declare class SharedCell<T = any> extends SharedObject<ISharedCellEvents<T>> implements ISharedCell<T>
```
**Extends**: [SharedObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/shared-object-base/sharedobject-class)<[ISharedCellEvents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/isharedcellevents-interface)

**Implements**: [ISharedCell](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/isharedcell-interface)

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | any |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#sharedcell-remarks)

### Creation

To create a `SharedCell`, call the static create method:

```
const myCell = SharedCell.create(this.runtime, id);
```
### Usage

The value stored in the cell can be set with the `.set()` method and retrieved with the `.get()` method:

```
myCell.set(3);
console.log(myCell.get()); // 3
```
The value must only be plain JS objects or `SharedObject` handles (e.g. to another DDS or Fluid object). In collaborative scenarios, the value is settled with a policy of _last write wins_.

The `.delete()` method will delete the stored value from the cell:

```
myCell.delete();
console.log(myCell.get()); // undefined
```
The `.empty()` method will check if the value is undefined.

```
if (myCell.empty()) {
  // myCell.get() will return undefined
} else {
  // myCell.get() will return a non-undefined value
}
```
### Eventing

`SharedCell` is an `EventEmitter`, and will emit events when other clients make modifications. You should register for these events and respond appropriately as the data is modified. `valueChanged` will be emitted in response to a `set`, and `delete` will be emitted in response to a `delete`.

## Constructors[](https://fluidframework.com#constructors)

| Constructor | Description |
|---|---|
| [(constructor)(id, runtime, attributes)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#_constructor_-constructor) | Constructs a new shared cell. If the object is non-local an id and service interfaces will be provided |

## Static Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#static-methods)

|---|---|---|
| [create(runtime, id)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#create-method) | [SharedCell](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class)<any> | Create a new shared cell |
| [getFactory()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#getfactory-method) | [IChannelFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/datastore-definitions/ichannelfactory-interface) | Get a factory for SharedCell to register with the data store. |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [delete()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#delete-method) | void | Delete the value from the cell. |
| [empty()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#empty-method) | boolean | Checks whether cell is empty or not. |
| [get()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#get-method) | [Serializable](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/datastore-definitions/serializable-typealias)<T> | undefined | Retrieves the cell value. |
| [initializeLocalCore()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#initializelocalcore-method) | void | Initialize a local instance of cell |
| [loadCore(storage)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#loadcore-method) | Promise<void> | |
| [onDisconnect()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#ondisconnect-method) | void | Call back on disconnect |
| [processCore(message, local, localOpMetadata)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#processcore-method) | void | Process a cell operation |

| [summarizeCore(serializer)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/cell/sharedcell-class#summarizecore-method) | [ISummaryTreeWithStats](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/runtime-definitions/isummarytreewithstats-interface) | Create a summary for the cell |

# @fluidframework/container-definitions Package | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/

This package contains the interfaces and types concerning the `Loader` and loading the `Container`.

## Interfaces[](https://fluidframework.com#interfaces)

| Interface | Alerts | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [ContainerWarning](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containerwarning-interface) | Represents warnings raised on container. | |
| [IAudience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iaudience-interface) | Audience represents all clients connected to the op stream, both read-only and read/write. | |
| [ICodeAllowList](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icodeallowlist-interface) | Code AllowListing Interface | |
| [ICodeDetailsLoader](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icodedetailsloader-interface) | Fluid code loader resolves a code module matching the document schema, i.e. code details, such as a package name and package version range. | |
| [ICodeLoader](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icodeloader-interface) | `Deprecated` | Code loading interface |
| [IConnectionDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iconnectiondetails-interface) | Contract representing the result of a newly established connection to the server for syncing deltas | |
| [IContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface) | The Host's view of the Container and its connection to storage | |
| [IContainerContext](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface) | The ContainerContext is a proxy standing between the Container and the Container's IRuntime. This allows the Container to terminate the connection to the IRuntime. Specifically, there is an event on Container, onContextChanged, which mean a new code proposal has been loaded, so the old IRuntime is no longer valid, as its ContainerContext has been revoked, and the Container has created a new ContainerContext. | |
| [IContainerEvents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainerevents-interface) | Events emitted by the Container "upwards" to the Loader and Host | |
| [IContainerLoadMode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainerloadmode-interface) | ||
| [IDeltaHandlerStrategy](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltahandlerstrategy-interface) | Interface used to define a strategy for handling incoming delta messages | |
| [IDeltaManager](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltamanager-interface) | Manages the transmission of ops between the runtime and storage. | |
| [IDeltaManagerEvents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltamanagerevents-interface) | Events emitted by the Delta Manager | |
| [IDeltaQueue](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface) | Queue of ops to be sent to or processed from storage | |
| [IDeltaQueueEvents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueueevents-interface) | Events emitted by a Delta Queue | |
| [IDeltaSender](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltasender-interface) | Contract supporting delivery of outbound messages to the server | |
| [IErrorBase](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ierrorbase-interface) | Base interface for all errors and warnings at container level | |
| [IFluidBrowserPackage](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidbrowserpackage-interface) | A Fluid package for specification for browser environments | |
| [IFluidBrowserPackageEnvironment](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidbrowserpackageenvironment-interface) | A specific Fluid package environment for browsers | |
| [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | Data structure used to describe the code to load on the Fluid document | |
| [IFluidCodeDetailsComparer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetailscomparer-interface) | Provides capability to compare Fluid code details. | |
| [IFluidCodeDetailsConfig](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetailsconfig-interface) | Package manager configuration. Provides a key value mapping of config values | |
| [IFluidCodeResolver](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcoderesolver-interface) | Fluid code resolvers take a Fluid code details, and resolve the full Fluid package including absolute urls for the browser file entries. The Fluid code resolver is coupled to a specific cdn and knows how to resolve the code detail for loading from that cdn. This include resolving to the most recent version of package that supports the provided code details. | |
| [IFluidModule](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodule-interface) | ||

| [IFluidPackage](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidpackage-interface) | Fluid-specific properties expected on a package to be loaded by the code loader. While compatible with the npm package format it is not necessary that that package is an npm package: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10065564/add-custom-metadata-or-config-to-package-json-is-it-valid](https://stackoverflow.com/questions/10065564/add-custom-metadata-or-config-to-package-json-is-it-valid) | |

# AttachState Enum | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum

The attachment state of some Fluid data (e.g. a container or data store), denoting whether it is uploaded to the service. The transition from detached to attached state is a one-way transition.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#attachstate-signature)

```
export declare enum AttachState
```
## Flags[](https://fluidframework.com#flags)

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| [Attached](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum#attached-enummember) | In attached state, the data has completed upload to the service. It can be accessed by other clients after reaching attached state. |
| [Attaching](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum#attaching-enummember) | In attaching state, the data has started the upload to the service, but has not yet completed. |
| [Detached](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum#detached-enummember) | In detached state, the data is only present on the local client's machine. It has not yet been uploaded to the service. |

### Attached[](https://fluidframework.com#attached-enummember)

In attached state, the data has completed upload to the service. It can be accessed by other clients after reaching attached state.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#attached-signature)

```
Attached = "Attached"
```
### Attaching[](https://fluidframework.com#attaching-enummember)

In attaching state, the data has started the upload to the service, but has not yet completed.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#attaching-signature)

```
Attaching = "Attaching"
```
### Detached[](https://fluidframework.com#detached-enummember)

In detached state, the data is only present on the local client's machine. It has not yet been uploaded to the service.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#detached-signature)

```
Detached = "Detached"
```

# ConnectionState Namespace | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/

Namespace for the different connection states a container can be in PLEASE NOTE: The sequence of the numerical values does no correspond to the typical connection state progression

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#connectionstate-signature)

```
export declare namespace ConnectionState
```
## Types[](https://fluidframework.com#types)

| TypeAlias | Alerts | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [CatchingUp](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/catchingup-typealias) | The container has an inbound connection only, and is catching up to the latest known state from the service. | |
| [Connected](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/connected-typealias) | The container is fully connected and syncing | |
| [Connecting](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/connecting-typealias) | `Deprecated` | See ConnectionState.CatchingUp, which is the new name for this state. |
| [Disconnected](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/disconnected-typealias) | The container is not connected to the delta server Note - When in this state the container may be about to reconnect, or may remain disconnected until explicitly told to connect. | |
| [EstablishingConnection](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/establishingconnection-typealias) | The container is disconnected but actively trying to establish a new connection PLEASE NOTE that this numerical value falls out of the order you may expect for this state |

# Connecting TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/connectionstate-namespace/connecting-typealias

See ConnectionState.CatchingUp, which is the new name for this state.

This API is deprecated and will be removed in a future release.

- This state itself is not gone, just being renamed. Please use ConnectionState.CatchingUp.

For up-to-date documentation, see the latest version (v2).

Disconnected TypeAlias

The container is not connected to the delta server Note - When in this state the container may be about to reconnect, or may remain disconnected until explicitly told to connect.

# ContainerErrorType Enum | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum

Different error types the Container may report out to the Host

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#containererrortype-signature)

```
export declare enum ContainerErrorType
```
## Flags[](https://fluidframework.com#flags)

| Flag | Description |
|---|---|
| [clientSessionExpiredError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#clientsessionexpirederror-enummember) | Error indicating an client session has expired. Currently this only happens when GC is allowed on a document and aids in safely deleting unused objects. |
| [dataCorruptionError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#datacorruptionerror-enummember) | Data loss error detected by Container / DeltaManager. Likely points to storage issue. |
| [dataProcessingError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#dataprocessingerror-enummember) | Error encountered when processing an operation. May correlate with data corruption. |
| [genericError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#genericerror-enummember) | Some error, most likely an exception caught by runtime and propagated to container as critical error |
| [throttlingError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#throttlingerror-enummember) | Throttling error from server. Server is busy and is asking not to reconnect for some time |
| [usageError](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/containererrortype-enum#usageerror-enummember) | Error indicating an API is being used improperly resulting in an invalid operation. |

### clientSessionExpiredError[](https://fluidframework.com#clientsessionexpirederror-enummember)

Error indicating an client session has expired. Currently this only happens when GC is allowed on a document and aids in safely deleting unused objects.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#clientsessionexpirederror-signature)

```
clientSessionExpiredError = "clientSessionExpiredError"
```
### dataCorruptionError[](https://fluidframework.com#datacorruptionerror-enummember)

Data loss error detected by Container / DeltaManager. Likely points to storage issue.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#datacorruptionerror-signature)

```
dataCorruptionError = "dataCorruptionError"
```
### dataProcessingError[](https://fluidframework.com#dataprocessingerror-enummember)

Error encountered when processing an operation. May correlate with data corruption.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#dataprocessingerror-signature)

```
dataProcessingError = "dataProcessingError"
```
### genericError[](https://fluidframework.com#genericerror-enummember)

Some error, most likely an exception caught by runtime and propagated to container as critical error

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#genericerror-signature)

```
genericError = "genericError"
```
### throttlingError[](https://fluidframework.com#throttlingerror-enummember)

Throttling error from server. Server is busy and is asking not to reconnect for some time

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#throttlingerror-signature)

```
throttlingError = "throttlingError"
```
### usageError[](https://fluidframework.com#usageerror-enummember)

Error indicating an API is being used improperly resulting in an invalid operation.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#usageerror-signature)

```
usageError = "usageError"

| [checkpointSequenceNumber](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iconnectiondetails-interface#checkpointsequencenumber-propertysignature) | number | undefined | Last known sequence number to ordering service at the time of connection It may lap actual last sequence number (quite a bit, if container is very active). But it's best information for client to figure out how far it is behind, at least for "read" connections. "write" connections may use own "join" op to similar information, that is likely to be more up-to-date. |

Container usually gets into this situation due to loss of connectivity. |
| [readOnlyInfo](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface#readonlyinfo-propertysignature) | [ReadOnlyInfo](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/readonlyinfo-typealias) | Tells if container is in read-only mode. Readonly state can be because of no storage write permission, or due to host forcing readonly mode for container. We do not differentiate here between no write access to storage vs. host disallowing changes to container - in all cases container runtime and data stores should respect readonly state and not allow local changes. ### isDirty[](https://fluidframework.com#isdirty-propertysignature)

Returns true if the container is dirty, i.e. there are user changes that has not been saved Closing container in this state results in data loss for user. Container usually gets into this situation due to loss of connectivity.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#isdirty-signature)

```
readonly isDirty: boolean;
```
**Type**: boolean

### readOnlyInfo[](https://fluidframework.com#readonlyinfo-propertysignature)

Tells if container is in read-only mode. Data stores should listen for "readonly" notifications and disallow user making changes to data stores. Readonly state can be because of no storage write permission, or due to host forcing readonly mode for container.

We do not differentiate here between no write access to storage vs. host disallowing changes to container - in all cases container runtime and data stores should respect readonly state and not allow local changes.

It is undefined if we have not yet established websocket connection and do not know if user has write access to a file.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#readonlyinfo-signature)

```
readonly readOnlyInfo: ReadOnlyInfo;
```
**Type**: [ReadOnlyInfo](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/readonlyinfo-typealias)

### resolvedUrl[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvedurl-propertysignature)

Represents the resolved url to the Container Will be undefined only when the container is in the [detatched](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum#detached-enummember) state.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvedurl-signature)

```
resolvedUrl: IResolvedUrl | undefined;
```
**Type**: [IResolvedUrl](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/driver-definitions/iresolvedurl-typealias) | undefined
