# IContainerContext Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface

The ContainerContext is a proxy standing between the Container and the Container's IRuntime. This allows the Container to terminate the connection to the IRuntime.

Specifically, there is an event on Container, onContextChanged, which mean a new code proposal has been loaded, so the old IRuntime is no longer valid, as its ContainerContext has been revoked, and the Container has created a new ContainerContext.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#icontainercontext-signature)

```
export interface IContainerContext extends IDisposable
```
**Extends**: IDisposable

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [attachState](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface#attachstate-propertysignature) | [AttachState](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/attachstate-enum) | Indicates the attachment state of the container to a host service. | |
| [audience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface#audience-propertysignature) | [IAudience](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iaudience-interface)| undefined | ||
| [baseSnapshot](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface#basesnapshot-propertysignature) | [ISnapshotTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/isnapshottree-interface)| undefined | ||
| [clientDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface#clientdetails-propertysignature) | [IClientDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/iclientdetails-interface) | ||
| [clientId](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainercontext-interface#clientid-propertysignature) | string | undefined | ||

### getSpecifiedCodeDetails[](https://fluidframework.com#getspecifiedcodedetails-methodsignature)

This method is provided as a migration tool for customers currently reading the code details from within the Container by directly accessing the Quorum proposals. The code details should not be accessed from within the Container as this requires coupling between the container contents and the code loader. Direct access to Quorum proposals will be removed in an upcoming release, and in a further future release this migration tool will be removed.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getspecifiedcodedetails-signature)

```
getSpecifiedCodeDetails?(): IFluidCodeDetails | undefined;
```
#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getspecifiedcodedetails-returns)

**Return type**: [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | undefined

### updateDirtyContainerState[](https://fluidframework.com#updatedirtycontainerstate-methodsignature)

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#updatedirtycontainerstate-signature)

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#updatedirtycontainerstate-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| dirty | boolean |

```
export interface IDeltaQueue<T> extends IEventProvider<IDeltaQueueEvents<T>>, IDisposable
```

|---|---|
| T |

|---|---|---|

| [length](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#length-propertysignature) | number | The number of messages remaining in the queue |
| [paused](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#paused-propertysignature) | boolean | Flag indicating whether or not the queue was paused |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [pause()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#pause-methodsignature) | Promise<void> | Pauses processing on the queue |
| [peek()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#peek-methodsignature) | T | undefined | Peeks at the next message in the queue |
| [resume()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#resume-methodsignature) | void | Resumes processing on the queue |
| [toArray()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#toarray-methodsignature) | T[] | Returns all the items in the queue as an array. Does not remove them from the queue. |
| [waitTillProcessingDone()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ideltaqueue-interface#waittillprocessingdone-methodsignature) | Promise<{ count: number; duration: number; }> | returns number of ops processed and time it took to process these ops. Zeros if queue did not process anything (had no messages, was paused or had hit an error before) |

| [message](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ierrorbase-interface#message-propertysignature) | string | See Error.message Privacy Note - This is a freeform string that we may not control in all cases (e.g. a dependency throws an error) If there are known cases where this contains privacy-sensitive data it will be tagged and included in the result of getTelemetryProperties. When logging, consider fetching it that way rather than straight from this field. | |

**Type**: string

### message[](https://fluidframework.com#message-propertysignature)

See Error.message Privacy Note - This is a freeform string that we may not control in all cases (e.g. a dependency throws an error) If there are known cases where this contains privacy-sensitive data it will be tagged and included in the result of getTelemetryProperties. When logging, consider fetching it that way rather than straight from this field.

# IFluidCodeDetailsComparer Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetailscomparer-interface

Provides capability to compare Fluid code details.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#ifluidcodedetailscomparer-signature)

```
export interface IFluidCodeDetailsComparer extends IProvideFluidCodeDetailsComparer
```
**Extends**: [IProvideFluidCodeDetailsComparer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iprovidefluidcodedetailscomparer-interface)

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [compare(a, b)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetailscomparer-interface#compare-methodsignature) | Promise<number | undefined> | Return a number representing the ascending sort order of the  Similar semantics to:  |
| [satisfies(candidate, constraint)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetailscomparer-interface#satisfies-methodsignature) | Promise<boolean> | Determines if the  Similar semantics to:  |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### compare[](https://fluidframework.com#compare-methodsignature)

Return a number representing the ascending sort order of the `a` and `b` code details; `< 0` if `a < b`. `= 0` if `a === b`. `> 0` if `a > b`. `undefined` if `a` is not comparable to `b`.

Similar semantics to: [Array.sort](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/JavaScript/Reference/Global_Objects/Array/sort#Description)

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#compare-signature)

```
compare(a: IFluidCodeDetails, b: IFluidCodeDetails): Promise<number | undefined>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#compare-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| a | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | |
| b | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#compare-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<number | undefined>

### satisfies[](https://fluidframework.com#satisfies-methodsignature)

Determines if the `candidate` code details satisfy the constraints specified in `constraint` code details.

Similar semantics to: [https://github.com/npm/node-semver#usage](https://github.com/npm/node-semver#usage)

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#satisfies-signature)

```
satisfies(candidate: IFluidCodeDetails, constraint: IFluidCodeDetails): Promise<boolean>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#satisfies-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| candidate | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | |
| constraint | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#satisfies-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<boolean>

---

# IFluidCodeResolver Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcoderesolver-interface

Fluid code resolvers take a Fluid code details, and resolve the full Fluid package including absolute urls for the browser file entries. The Fluid code resolver is coupled to a specific cdn and knows how to resolve the code detail for loading from that cdn. This include resolving to the most recent version of package that supports the provided code details.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#ifluidcoderesolver-signature)

```
export interface IFluidCodeResolver
```
## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [resolveCodeDetails(details)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcoderesolver-interface#resolvecodedetails-methodsignature) | Promise< [IResolvedFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iresolvedfluidcodedetails-interface)> | Resolves a Fluid code details into a form that can be loaded |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### resolveCodeDetails[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvecodedetails-methodsignature)

Resolves a Fluid code details into a form that can be loaded

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvecodedetails-signature)

```
resolveCodeDetails(details: IFluidCodeDetails): Promise<IResolvedFluidCodeDetails>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvecodedetails-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| details | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | The Fluid code details to resolve |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#resolvecodedetails-returns)

- A IResolvedFluidCodeDetails where the resolvedPackage's Fluid file entries are absolute urls, and an optional resolvedPackageCacheId if the loaded package should be cached.

**Return type**: Promise<[IResolvedFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iresolvedfluidcodedetails-interface)>

# IFluidModuleWithDetails Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodulewithdetails-interface

Encapsulates a module entry point with corresponding code details.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#ifluidmodulewithdetails-signature)

```
export interface IFluidModuleWithDetails
```
## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [details](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodulewithdetails-interface#details-propertysignature) | [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface) | Code details associated with the module. Represents a document schema this module supports. If the code loader implements the @fluidframework/core-interfaces#IFluidCodeDetailsComparerinterface, it'll be called to determine whether the module code details satisfy the new code proposal in the quorum. |
| [module](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodulewithdetails-interface#module-propertysignature) | [IFluidModule](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodule-interface) | Fluid code module that implements the runtime factory needed to instantiate the container runtime. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### details[](https://fluidframework.com#details-propertysignature)

Code details associated with the module. Represents a document schema this module supports. If the code loader implements the *@fluidframework/core-interfaces#IFluidCodeDetailsComparer* interface, it'll be called to determine whether the module code details satisfy the new code proposal in the quorum.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#details-signature)

```
details: IFluidCodeDetails;
```
**Type**: [IFluidCodeDetails](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidcodedetails-interface)

### module[](https://fluidframework.com#module-propertysignature)

Fluid code module that implements the runtime factory needed to instantiate the container runtime.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#module-signature)

```
module: IFluidModule;
```
**Type**: [IFluidModule](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/ifluidmodule-interface)

# ILoader Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iloader-interface

The Runtime's view of the Loader, used for loading Containers

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#iloader-signature)

```
export interface ILoader extends IFluidRouter, Partial<IProvideLoader>
```
**Extends**: [IFluidRouter](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/ifluidrouter-interface), Partial<[IProvideLoader](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iprovideloader-interface)

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [resolve(request, pendingLocalState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iloader-interface#resolve-methodsignature) | Promise< [IContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface)> | Resolves the resource specified by the URL + headers contained in the request object to the underlying container that will resolve the request. An analogy for this is resolve is a DNS resolve of a Fluid container. Request then executes a request against the server found from the resolve step. |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### resolve[](https://fluidframework.com#resolve-methodsignature)

Resolves the resource specified by the URL + headers contained in the request object to the underlying container that will resolve the request.

An analogy for this is resolve is a DNS resolve of a Fluid container. Request then executes a request against the server found from the resolve step.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#resolve-signature)

```
resolve(request: IRequest, pendingLocalState?: string): Promise<IContainer>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#resolve-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| request | [IRequest](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/irequest-interface) | ||
| pendingLocalState | optional | string |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#resolve-returns)

**Return type**: Promise<[IContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface)>

# IRuntime Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface

The IRuntime represents an instantiation of a code package within a Container. Primarily held by the ContainerContext to be able to interact with the running instance of the Container.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#iruntime-signature)

```
export interface IRuntime extends IDisposable
```
**Extends**: IDisposable

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [createSummary(blobRedirectTable)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#createsummary-methodsignature) | [ISummaryTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/isummarytree-interface) | Create a summary. Used when attaching or serializing a detached container. |
| [getPendingLocalState()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#getpendinglocalstate-methodsignature) | unknown | Get pending local state in a serializable format to be given back to a newly loaded container |
| [notifyAttaching(snapshot)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#notifyattaching-methodsignature) | void | Notify runtime that container is moving to "Attaching" state |
| [process(message, local, context)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#process-methodsignature) | any | Processes the given op (message) |
| [processSignal(message, local)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#processsignal-methodsignature) | any | Processes the given signal |
| [request(request)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#request-methodsignature) | Promise< [IResponse](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/iresponse-interface)> | Executes a request against the runtime |
| [setAttachState(attachState)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#setattachstate-methodsignature) | void | Propagate the container state when container is attaching or attached. |
| [setConnectionState(connected, clientId)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/iruntime-interface#setconnectionstate-methodsignature) | any | Notifies the runtime of a change in the connection state |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### createSummary[](https://fluidframework.com#createsummary-methodsignature)

Create a summary. Used when attaching or serializing a detached container.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#createsummary-signature)

```
createSummary(blobRedirectTable?: Map<string, string>): ISummaryTree;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#createsummary-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| blobRedirectTable | optional | Map<string, string> | A table passed during the attach process. While detached, blob upload is supported using IDs generated locally. After attach, these IDs cannot be used, so this table maps the old local IDs to the new storage IDs so requests can be redirected. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#createsummary-returns)

**Return type**: [ISummaryTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/isummarytree-interface)

### getPendingLocalState[](https://fluidframework.com#getpendinglocalstate-methodsignature)

# ISnapshotTreeWithBlobContents Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/isnapshottreewithblobcontents-interface

This is used when we rehydrate a container from the snapshot. Here we put the blob contents in separate property: blobContents. This is used as the ContainerContext's base snapshot when attaching.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#isnapshottreewithblobcontents-signature)

```
export interface ISnapshotTreeWithBlobContents extends ISnapshotTree
```
**Extends**: [ISnapshotTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/protocol-definitions/isnapshottree-interface)

|---|---|---|
| [blobsContents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/isnapshottreewithblobcontents-interface#blobscontents-propertysignature) | { [path: string]: ArrayBufferLike; } | |
| [trees](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/isnapshottreewithblobcontents-interface#trees-propertysignature) | {         [path: string]: [ISnapshotTreeWithBlobContents](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/isnapshottreewithblobcontents-interface);     } |

```
        [path: string]: ArrayBufferLike;
    };
```

```
        [path: string]: ISnapshotTreeWithBlobContents;
```

## Functions[](https://fluidframework.com#functions)

| Function | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [waitContainerToCatchUp(container)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-loader/#waitcontainertocatchup-function) | Promise<boolean> | Waits until container connects to delta storage and gets up-to-date Useful when resolving URIs and hitting 404, due to container being loaded from (stale) snapshot and not being up to date. Host may chose to wait in such case and retry resolving URI. Warning: Will wait infinitely for connection to establish if there is no connection. May result in deadlock if Container.disconnect() is called and never followed by a call to Container.connect(). |

## Function Details[](https://fluidframework.com#function-details)

### waitContainerToCatchUp[](https://fluidframework.com#waitcontainertocatchup-function)

Waits until container connects to delta storage and gets up-to-date Useful when resolving URIs and hitting 404, due to container being loaded from (stale) snapshot and not being up to date. Host may chose to wait in such case and retry resolving URI. Warning: Will wait infinitely for connection to establish if there is no connection. May result in deadlock if Container.disconnect() is called and never followed by a call to Container.connect().

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#waitcontainertocatchup-signature)

```
export declare function waitContainerToCatchUp(container: IContainer): Promise<boolean>;
```
#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#waitcontainertocatchup-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| container | [IContainer](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-definitions/icontainer-interface) |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#waitcontainertocatchup-returns)

true: container is up to date, it processed all the ops that were know at the time of first connection false: storage does not provide indication of how far the client is. Container processed all the ops known to it, but it maybe still behind.

**Return type**: Promise<boolean>

#### Error Handling[](https://fluidframework.com#waitcontainertocatchup-throws)

an error beginning with `"Container closed"` if the container is closed before it catches up.

# IDetachedBlobStorage TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-loader/idetachedblobstorage-typealias

Subset of IDocumentStorageService which only supports createBlob() and readBlob(). This is used to support blobs in detached containers.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#idetachedblobstorage-signature)

```
export declare type IDetachedBlobStorage = Pick<IDocumentStorageService, "createBlob" | "readBlob"> & {
    size: number;
    getBlobIds(): string[];
};
```

# IEnqueueSummarizeOptions Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/ienqueuesummarizeoptions-interface

Options to use when enqueueing a summarize attempt.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#ienqueuesummarizeoptions-signature)

```
export interface IEnqueueSummarizeOptions extends IOnDemandSummarizeOptions
```
**Extends**: [IOnDemandSummarizeOptions](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/iondemandsummarizeoptions-interface)

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [afterSequenceNumber](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/ienqueuesummarizeoptions-interface#aftersequencenumber-propertysignature) | `optional` | number | If specified, The summarize attempt will not occur until after this sequence number. |
| [override](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/ienqueuesummarizeoptions-interface#override-propertysignature) | `optional` | boolean | True to override the existing enqueued summarize attempt if there is one. This will guarantee that this attempt gets enqueued. If override is false, than an existing enqueued summarize attempt will block a new one from being enqueued. There can only be one enqueued at a time. Defaults to false. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### afterSequenceNumber[](https://fluidframework.com#aftersequencenumber-propertysignature)

If specified, The summarize attempt will not occur until after this sequence number.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#aftersequencenumber-signature)

```
readonly afterSequenceNumber?: number;
```
**Type**: number

### override[](https://fluidframework.com#override-propertysignature)

True to override the existing enqueued summarize attempt if there is one. This will guarantee that this attempt gets enqueued. If override is false, than an existing enqueued summarize attempt will block a new one from being enqueued. There can only be one enqueued at a time. Defaults to false.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#override-signature)

```
readonly override?: boolean;
```
**Type**: boolean

# ISummary Interface | Fluid Framework

A single summary which can be tracked as it goes through its life cycle. The life cycle is: Local to Broadcast to Acked/Nacked.

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| [waitBroadcast()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/isummary-interface#waitbroadcast-methodsignature) | Promise< [ISummaryOpMessage](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/isummaryopmessage-interface)> |


## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### waitAckNack[](https://fluidframework.com#waitacknack-methodsignature)

# ScheduleManager Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/schedulemanager-class

This class has the following responsibilities: 1. It tracks batches as we process ops and raises "batchBegin" and "batchEnd" events. As part of it, it validates batch correctness (i.e. no system ops in the middle of batch) 2. It creates instance of ScheduleManagerCore that ensures we never start processing ops from batch unless all ops of the batch are in.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#schedulemanager-signature)

```
export declare class ScheduleManager
```

# SubmitSummaryResult TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/container-runtime/submitsummaryresult-typealias

Strict type representing result of a submitSummary attempt. The result consists of 4 possible stages, each with its own data. The data is cumulative, so each stage will contain the data from the previous stages. If the final "submitted" stage is not reached, the result may contain the error object. Stages: 1. "base" - stopped before the summary tree was even generated, and the result only contains the base data 2. "generate" - the summary tree was generated, and the result will contain that tree + stats 3. "upload" - the summary was uploaded to storage, and the result contains the server-provided handle 4. "submit" - the summarize op was submitted, and the result contains the op client sequence number.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#submitsummaryresult-signature)

```
export declare type SubmitSummaryResult = IBaseSummarizeResult | IGenerateSummaryTreeResult | IUploadSummaryResult | ISubmitSummaryOpResult;
```

---

# FluidObjectKeys TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/fluidobjectkeys-typealias

This utility type creates a type that is the union of all keys on the generic type which implement the FluidObject pattern.

See [FluidObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/core-interfaces/fluidobject-typealias)

For example `FluidObjectKeys<IFoo & IBar>` would result in `"IFoo" | "IBar"`

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#fluidobjectkeys-signature)

```
export declare type FluidObjectKeys<T> = keyof FluidObject<T>;
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| T |

# DriverPreCheckInfo Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/driver-definitions/driverprecheckinfo-interface

Information that can be returned by a lightweight, seperately exported driver function. Used to preanalyze a URL for driver compatibility and preload information.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#driverprecheckinfo-signature)

```
export interface DriverPreCheckInfo
```
## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [codeDetailsHint](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/driver-definitions/driverprecheckinfo-interface#codedetailshint-propertysignature) | `optional` | string | A code details hint that can potentially be used to prefetch container code prior to having a snapshot. |
| [criticalBootDomains](https://fluidframework.com/docs/v1/api/driver-definitions/driverprecheckinfo-interface#criticalbootdomains-propertysignature) | `optional` | string[] | Domains that will be connected to on the critical boot path. Hosts can choose to preconnect to these for improved performance. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### codeDetailsHint[](https://fluidframework.com#codedetailshint-propertysignature)

A code details hint that can potentially be used to prefetch container code prior to having a snapshot.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#codedetailshint-signature)

```
codeDetailsHint?: string;
```
**Type**: string

### criticalBootDomains[](https://fluidframework.com#criticalbootdomains-propertysignature)

Domains that will be connected to on the critical boot path. Hosts can choose to preconnect to these for improved performance.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#criticalbootdomains-signature)

```
criticalBootDomains?: string[];
```
**Type**: string[]

# IsUnion TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/isunion-typealias

```
export type IsUnion<T, T2 = T> = T extends unknown ? [T2] extends [T] ? false : true : "error";
```

# IterableTreeArrayContent Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/iterabletreearraycontent-class

Used to insert iterable content into a [TreeArrayNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treearraynode-interface). Use *(TreeArrayNode:variable).spread* to create an instance of this type.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#iterabletreearraycontent-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export declare class IterableTreeArrayContent<T> implements Iterable<T>
```
**Implements**: Iterable<T>

|---|---|
| T |

```
/** @sealed */
export interface ITree extends ViewableTree, IFluidLoadable
```
**Extends**: [ViewableTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/viewabletree-interface), [IFluidLoadable](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/ifluidloadable-interface)

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#itree-remarks)

Allows storing and collaboratively editing schema-aware hierarchial data.

# ITreeConfigurationOptions Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/itreeconfigurationoptions-interface

Options when constructing a tree view.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#itreeconfigurationoptions-signature)

```
export interface ITreeConfigurationOptions
```
## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Modifiers | Default Value | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [enableSchemaValidation](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/itreeconfigurationoptions-interface#enableschemavalidation-propertysignature) | `optional` | `false`. | boolean | If `true`, the tree will perform additional validation of content against its stored schema and throw an error if the new content doesn't match the expected schema. |
| [preventAmbiguity](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/itreeconfigurationoptions-interface#preventambiguity-propertysignature) | `optional`,`readonly` | `false`. | boolean | A flag used to opt into strict rules ensuring that the schema avoids cases which can make the type of nodes ambiguous when importing or exporting data. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### enableSchemaValidation[](https://fluidframework.com#enableschemavalidation-propertysignature)

If `true`, the tree will perform additional validation of content against its stored schema and throw an error if the new content doesn't match the expected schema.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#enableschemavalidation-signature)

```
enableSchemaValidation?: boolean;
```
**Type**: boolean

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#enableschemavalidation-remarks)

Currently most cases already have some schema validation, so this is mainly for additional validation which may be useful when debugging issues, working with untyped APIs, or when the small performance overhead is a non-issue.

Enabling schema validation has a performance penalty when inserting new content into the tree because additional checks are done. Enable this option only in scenarios where you are ok with that operation being a bit slower.

For additional validation in more cases, see [ForestTypeExpensiveDebug](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/#foresttypeexpensivedebug-variable).

### preventAmbiguity[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-propertysignature)

A flag used to opt into strict rules ensuring that the schema avoids cases which can make the type of nodes ambiguous when importing or exporting data.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-signature)

```
readonly preventAmbiguity?: boolean;
```
**Type**: boolean

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-remarks)

When this is true, it ensures that the compile time type safety for data when constructing nodes is sufficient to ensure that the runtime behavior will not give node data ambiguity errors.

This ensures that the canonical JSON-like representation of all unions in the tree are lossless and unambiguous. This canonical JSON-like representation consists of arrays, plain old JavaScript objects with string keys, booleans, numbers (excluding NaN, -0 and infinities), strings, null and *@fluidframework/core-interfaces#IFluidHandle*s. It is compatible with the node creation APIs (such as schema class constructors) and is also compatible with JSON assuming any IFluidHandles get special handling (since they are not JSON compatible). Currently these cases can cause ambiguity in a union:

- More than one ArrayNode type: it's impossible to tell which array type is intended in the case of empty arrays (`[]`).

- More than one MapNode type: it's impossible to tell which map type is intended in the case of an empty map (`{}`).

- Both a MapNode and an ArrayNode: this case is not a problem for the canonical JSON representation, but is an issue when constructing from an Iterable, which is supported for both MapNode and ArrayNode.

- Both a MapNode and an ObjectNode: when the input is valid for the ObjectNode, the current parser always considers it ambiguous with being a MapNode.

- ObjectNodes which have fields (required or optional) which include all required fields of another ObjectNode: currently each ObjectNode is differentiated by the presence of its required fields.

This check is conservative: some complex cases may error if the current simple algorithm cannot show no ambiguity is possible. This check may become more permissive over time.

#### Usage[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-examples)

##### Example 1[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-example1)

Ambiguous schema (with `preventAmbiguity: false`), and how to disambiguate it using [Unhydrated](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/unhydrated-typealias) nodes:

```
const schemaFactory = new SchemaFactory("com.example");
class Feet extends schemaFactory.object("Feet", { length: schemaFactory.number }) {}
class Meters extends schemaFactory.object("Meters", { length: schemaFactory.number }) {}
const config = new TreeViewConfiguration({
	// This combination of schema can lead to ambiguous cases and will error if `preventAmbiguity` is true.
	schema: [Feet, Meters],
	preventAmbiguity: false,
});
const view = tree.viewWith(config);
// This is invalid since it is ambiguous which type of node is being constructed:
// view.initialize({ length: 5 });
// To work, an explicit type can be provided by using an {@link Unhydrated} Node:
view.initialize(new Meters({ length: 5 }));
```
##### Example 2[](https://fluidframework.com#preventambiguity-example2)

Schema disambiguated by adjusting field names, validated with `preventAmbiguity: true:`

```
const schemaFactory = new SchemaFactory("com.example");
class Feet extends schemaFactory.object("Feet", { length: schemaFactory.number }) {}
class Meters extends schemaFactory.object("Meters", {
	// To avoid ambiguity when parsing unions of Feet and Meters, this renames the length field to "meters".
	// To preserve compatibility with existing data from the ambiguous case,
	// `{ key: "length" }` is set, so when persisted in the tree "length" is used as the field name.
	meters: schemaFactory.required(schemaFactory.number, { key: "length" }),
}) {}
const config = new TreeViewConfiguration({
	// This combination of schema is not ambiguous because `Feet` and `Meters` have different required keys.
	schema: [Feet, Meters],
	preventAmbiguity: true,
});
const view = tree.viewWith(config);
// This now works, since the field is sufficient to determine this is a `Meters` node.
view.initialize({ meters: 5 });
```

# JsonAsTree Namespace | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/

Utilities for storing JSON data in [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class)s.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonastree-signature)

```
export declare namespace JsonAsTree
```
## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonastree-remarks)

Schema which replicate the JSON data model with [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class)s.

This allows JSON to be losslessly round-tripped through a tree with the following limitations:

- Only information that would be preserved by JSON.parse is preserved. This means (among other things) that numbers are limited to JavasScript's numeric precision.

- The order of fields on an object is not preserved. The resulting order is arbitrary.

JSON data can be imported from JSON into this format using `JSON.parse` then [importConcise(schema, data)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treebeta-interface#importconcise-methodsignature) with the [Tree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/#tree-variable) schema.

## Classes[](https://fluidframework.com#classes)

| Class | Alerts | Modifiers | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Array](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/array-class) | `Alpha` | `sealed` | Arbitrary JSON array as a [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class). |
| [JsonObject](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/jsonobject-class) | `Alpha` | `sealed` | Arbitrary JSON object as a [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class). |

## Types[](https://fluidframework.com#types)

| TypeAlias | Alerts | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [_RecursiveArrayWorkaroundJsonArray](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/u_recursivearrayworkaroundjsonarray-typealias) | `System` | D.ts bug workaround, see [FixRecursiveArraySchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/fixrecursivearrayschema-typealias). |
| [Primitive](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/primitive-typealias) | `Alpha` | [AllowedTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/allowedtypes-typealias)for primitives types allowed in JSON. |
| [Tree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/tree-typealias) | `Alpha` | [AllowedTypes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/allowedtypes-typealias)for any content allowed in the[JsonAsTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/)domain. |

### _APIExtractorWorkaroundObjectBase[](https://fluidframework.com#_apiextractorworkaroundobjectbase-variable)

```
const tree = TreeBeta.importConcise(JsonAsTree.Union, { example: { nested: true }, value: 5 });
```

# Array Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/array-class

Arbitrary JSON array as a [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class).

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#array-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
class Array extends _APIExtractorWorkaroundArrayBase
```
**Extends**: _APIExtractorWorkaroundArrayBase

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#array-remarks)

This can be imported using [importConcise(schema, data)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treebeta-interface#importconcise-methodsignature).

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#array-example)

```
// Due to TypeScript restrictions on recursive types, the constructor can be somewhat limiting.
const usingConstructor = new JsonAsTree.Array(["a", 0, new JsonAsTree.Array([1])]);
// Using `importConcise` can work better for JSON data:
const imported = TreeBeta.importConcise(JsonAsTree.Array, ["a", 0, [1]]);
// Node API is like an Array:
const inner: JsonAsTree.Tree = imported[2];
assert(Tree.is(inner, JsonAsTree.Array));
const leaf = inner[0];
```

---

# JsonObject Class | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonastree-namespace/jsonobject-class

Arbitrary JSON object as a [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class).

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonobject-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
class JsonObject extends _APIExtractorWorkaroundObjectBase
```
**Extends**: _APIExtractorWorkaroundObjectBase

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonobject-remarks)

API of the tree node is more aligned with an es6 map than a JS object using its properties like a map.

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonobject-example)

```
// Due to TypeScript restrictions on recursive types, the constructor and be somewhat limiting.
const fromArray = new JsonAsTreeObject([["a", 0]]);
// Using `importConcise` can work better for JSON data:
const imported = TreeBeta.importConcise(JsonAsTree.Object, { a: 0 });
// Node API is like a Map:
const value = imported.get("a");
```

---

# JsonCompatible TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsoncompatible-typealias

Use for Json compatible data.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsoncompatible-signature)

```
export type JsonCompatible<TExtra = never> = string | number | boolean | null | JsonCompatible<TExtra>[] | JsonCompatibleObject<TExtra> | TExtra;
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| TExtra | never | Type permitted in addition to the normal JSON types. Commonly used for to allow @fluidframework/core-interfaces#IFluidHandlewithin the otherwise JSON compatible content. |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#jsoncompatible-remarks)

This does not robustly forbid non json comparable data via type checking, but instead mostly restricts access to it.

# JsonNodeSchemaBase Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonnodeschemabase-interface

Base interface for node schemas represented in [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core) format.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonnodeschemabase-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface JsonNodeSchemaBase<TNodeKind extends NodeKind, TJsonSchemaType extends JsonSchemaType>
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| TNodeKind | [NodeKind](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodekind-enum) | |
| TJsonSchemaType | [JsonSchemaType](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonschematype-typealias) |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Alerts | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [_treeNodeSchemaKind](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonnodeschemabase-interface#_treenodeschemakind-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `readonly` | TNodeKind | Kind of [TreeNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschema-typealias)this JSON Schema entry represents. |
| [description](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonnodeschemabase-interface#description-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `optional`,`readonly` | string | undefined | Description of the node schema. |
| [type](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonnodeschemabase-interface#type-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `readonly` | TJsonSchemaType | JSON entity type. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### _treeNodeSchemaKind[](https://fluidframework.com#_treenodeschemakind-propertysignature)

Kind of [TreeNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschema-typealias) this JSON Schema entry represents.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#_treenodeschemakind-signature)

```
readonly _treeNodeSchemaKind: TNodeKind;
```
**Type**: TNodeKind

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#_treenodeschemakind-remarks)

There is not a 1:1 mapping between [TreeNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschema-typealias) types and JSON Schema types. This is used to disambiguate the type of [TreeNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschema-typealias) this JSON Schema maps to.

Note: This property name is not a part of the JSON Schema spec. This is a Fluid-specific extension.

### description[](https://fluidframework.com#description-propertysignature)

Description of the node schema.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#description-signature)

```
readonly description?: string | undefined;
```
**Type**: string | undefined

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#description-remarks)

Derived from [description](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodeschemametadata-interface#description-propertysignature).

#### See Also[](https://fluidframework.com#description-see-also)

### type[](https://fluidframework.com#type-propertysignature)

JSON entity type.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#type-signature)

```
readonly type: TJsonSchemaType;
```
**Type**: TJsonSchemaType

# JsonRefPath TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonrefpath-typealias

Reference string pointing to a definition in the schema. Should be the fully-qualified [identifier](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschemacore-interface#identifier-propertysignature).

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonrefpath-signature)

```
export type JsonRefPath = `#/$defs/${JsonSchemaId}`;
```
## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonrefpath-remarks)

Of the form `#/$defs/<schema-identifier>`, where the `schema-identifier` is the fully-qualified [identifier](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschemacore-interface#identifier-propertysignature).

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonrefpath-example)

Schema `com.myapp.foo` would be referenced via `#/$defs/com.myapp.foo`.

---

# JsonSchemaType TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

To use, import via `fluid-framework/alpha`.

For more information about our API support guarantees, see [here](https://fluidframework.com/docs/build/releases-and-apitags/#api-support-levels).

# JsonStringKeyPatternProperties Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonstringkeypatternproperties-interface

Types allowed in map / record nodes.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsonstringkeypatternproperties-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface JsonStringKeyPatternProperties
```
## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Alerts | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| ["^.*$"](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonstringkeypatternproperties-interface#__.___-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | [JsonFieldSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonfieldschema-typealias) | This format allows for any string key that can appear in tree schema in a way that is JSON schema compatible, but restricts the value to the specified allowed types of the value to only those specified. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### "^.*$"[](https://fluidframework.com#__.___-propertysignature)

This format allows for any string key that can appear in tree schema in a way that is JSON schema compatible, but restricts the value to the specified allowed types of the value to only those specified.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#__.___-signature)

```
"^.*$": JsonFieldSchema;
```
**Type**: [JsonFieldSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonfieldschema-typealias)

# JsonTreeSchema TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsontreeschema-typealias

[JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/draft/2020-12/json-schema-core) representation of a tree schema.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#jsontreeschema-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export type JsonTreeSchema = JsonFieldSchema & {
    readonly $defs: Record<JsonSchemaId, JsonNodeSchema>;
};
```
## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#jsontreeschema-remarks)

Includes the complete set of definitions reachable from the "root" schema.

Note: This representation only uses a limited subset of supported JSON Schema features. It is scoped to a format that can be used to sufficiently represent supported SharedTree schema.

Also note that this schema format contains Fluid-specific extensions, such as the [_treeNodeSchemaKind](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsonnodeschemabase-interface#_treenodeschemakind-propertysignature) property, meaning that it is not a *strict* subset. When using these schemas with validation tools (for example, [https://ajv.js.org/](https://ajv.js.org/)), you will need to opt out of *strict* validation to ensure extra properties are allowed.

---

# KeyEncodingOptions Enum | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/keyencodingoptions-enum

Options for how to encode keys in a tree.

This type is "input," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not read from it. Future versions of this type may add optional members or make typing of members more general.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#keyencodingoptions-signature)

```
export declare enum KeyEncodingOptions
```
## Flags[](https://fluidframework.com#flags)

| Flag | Alerts | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [allStoredKeys](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/keyencodingoptions-enum#allstoredkeys-enummember) | `Beta` | Use stored keys, and include [Unknown optional fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature). |
| [knownStoredKeys](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/keyencodingoptions-enum#knownstoredkeys-enummember) | `Beta` | Use stored keys but do not include [unknown optional fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature). |
| [usePropertyKeys](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/keyencodingoptions-enum#usepropertykeys-enummember) | `Beta` | Use property keys. |

### allStoredKeys[](https://fluidframework.com#allstoredkeys-enummember)

Use stored keys, and include [Unknown optional fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature).

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#allstoredkeys-signature)

```
allStoredKeys = "allStoredKeys"
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#allstoredkeys-remarks)

Currently only supported for export.

### knownStoredKeys[](https://fluidframework.com#knownstoredkeys-enummember)

Use stored keys but do not include [unknown optional fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature).

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#knownstoredkeys-signature)

```
knownStoredKeys = "knownStoredKeys"
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#knownstoredkeys-remarks)

Supported for import and export. For export, this omits unknown optional fields. For import, any unexpected fields are errors, regardless of [allowUnknownOptionalFields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature).

### usePropertyKeys[](https://fluidframework.com#usepropertykeys-enummember)

Use property keys.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#usepropertykeys-signature)

```
usePropertyKeys = "usePropertyKeys"
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#usepropertykeys-remarks)

Supported for import and export. [Unknown optional fields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) will be omitted when using property keys.

# LabelTree Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface

A tree representing the nesting structure of transaction labels.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#labeltree-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface LabelTree
```
## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#labeltree-remarks)

Each transaction contributes a node whose [label](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface#label-propertysignature) is its [label](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/runtransactionparams-interface#label-propertysignature) (or `undefined` if no label was provided). When transactions are nested, inner transaction nodes become [sublabels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface#sublabels-propertysignature) of outer ones.

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Alerts | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [label](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface#label-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | unknown | The label for this transaction, or `undefined`if no label was provided. |
| [sublabels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface#sublabels-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | [LabelTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface)[] | The label trees of any nested transactions within this one. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### label[](https://fluidframework.com#label-propertysignature)

The label for this transaction, or `undefined` if no label was provided.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#label-signature)

```
label: unknown;
```
**Type**: unknown

### sublabels[](https://fluidframework.com#sublabels-propertysignature)

The label trees of any nested transactions within this one.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#sublabels-signature)

```
sublabels: LabelTree[];
```
**Type**: [LabelTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface)[]

---

# LazyItem TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/lazyitem-typealias

An "eager" or "lazy" Item in a `FlexList`. Lazy items are wrapped in a function to allow referring to themselves before they are declared. This makes recursive and co-recursive items possible.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#lazyitem-signature)

```
export type LazyItem<Item = unknown> = Item | (() => Item);
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Item | unknown |

---

# LeafSchema Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/leafschema-interface

A [TreeNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschema-typealias) for a [TreeLeafValue](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treeleafvalue-typealias).

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#leafschema-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface LeafSchema<Name extends string, T extends TreeLeafValue> extends TreeNodeSchemaNonClass<`com.fluidframework.leaf.${Name}`, NodeKind.Leaf, T, T, true>
```
**Extends**: [TreeNodeSchemaNonClass](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschemanonclass-typealias)<`com.fluidframework.leaf.${Name}`, [NodeKind.Leaf](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodekind-enum#leaf-enummember), T, T, true>

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| Name | string | |
| T | [TreeLeafValue](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treeleafvalue-typealias) |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#leafschema-remarks)

This is just a more specific alias for a particular [TreeNodeSchemaNonClass](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenodeschemanonclass-typealias). It only exists to make the API (particularly errors, IntelliSense, and generated .d.ts files) more readable.

See [SchemaFactory](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class) and its various properties for actual leaf schema objects.

# Listenable Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface

An object which allows the registration of listeners so that subscribers can be notified when an event happens.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#listenable-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface Listenable<TListeners extends object>
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| TListeners | object |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| [off(eventName, listener)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface#off-methodsignature) | void | Deregister an event listener. |
| [on(eventName, listener)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface#on-methodsignature) | [Off](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/off-typealias) | Register an event listener. |

## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### off[](https://fluidframework.com#off-methodsignature)

Deregister an event listener.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#off-signature)

```
off<K extends keyof Listeners<TListeners>>(eventName: K, listener: TListeners[K]): void;
```
##### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters-1)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| K | keyof [Listeners](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listeners-typealias)<TListeners> |

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#off-remarks)

If `listener` is not currently registered, this method will have no effect.

Listeners may also be deregistered by calling the [deregistration function](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/off-typealias) returned when they are [registered](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface#on-methodsignature).

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#off-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| eventName | K | The name of the event. |
| listener | TListeners[K] | The listener function to remove from the current set of event listeners. |

### on[](https://fluidframework.com#on-methodsignature)

Register an event listener.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#on-signature)

```
on<K extends keyof Listeners<TListeners>>(eventName: K, listener: TListeners[K]): Off;
```
##### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters-2)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| K | keyof [Listeners](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listeners-typealias)<TListeners> |

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#on-remarks)

Registering the exact same `listener` object for the same event more than once will throw an error. If registering the same listener for the same event multiple times is desired, consider using a wrapper function for the second subscription.

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#on-parameters)

| Parameter | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|
| eventName | K | The name of the event. |
| listener | TListeners[K] | The listener function to run when the event is fired. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#on-returns)

A [function](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/off-typealias) which will deregister the listener when called. Calling the deregistration function more than once will have no effect.

Listeners may also be deregistered by passing the listener to [off()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface#off-methodsignature).

**Return type**: [Off](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/off-typealias)

---

# Listeners TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listeners-typealias

Used to specify the kinds of events emitted by a [Listenable](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listenable-interface).

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#listeners-signature)

```
export type Listeners<T extends object> = {
    [P in (string | symbol) & keyof T as IsListener<T[P]> extends true ? P : never]: T[P];
};
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | object |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#listeners-remarks)

Any object type is a valid [Listeners](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/listeners-typealias), but only the [event-like](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/islistener-typealias) properties of that type will be included.

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#listeners-example)

```
interface MyEvents {
  load: (user: string, data: IUserData) => void;
  error: (errorCode: number) => void;
}
```

---

# LocalChangeMetadata Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface

Information about a change that has been applied by the local client.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#localchangemetadata-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface LocalChangeMetadata extends CommitMetadata
```
**Extends**: [CommitMetadata](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/commitmetadata-interface)

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Alerts | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| [isLocal](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface#islocal-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `readonly` | true | Whether the change was made on the local machine/client or received from a remote client. |
| [label](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface#label-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `optional`,`readonly` | unknown | Optional label provided by the user when commit was created. This can be used by undo/redo to group or classify edits. |
| [labels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface#labels-propertysignature) | `Alpha` | `readonly` | [TransactionLabels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/transactionlabels-typealias) | A set of [labels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/runtransactionparams-interface#label-propertysignature)for all transactions (nested or otherwise) that made up this change. This can be used to identify, group, or filter changes — for example, to decide whether a change should be included in an undo/redo stack. |

## Methods[](https://fluidframework.com#methods)

| Method | Alerts | Return Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| [getChange()](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface#getchange-methodsignature) | `Alpha` | [JsonCompatibleReadOnly](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsoncompatiblereadonly-typealias) | Returns a serializable object that encodes the change. |
| [getRevertible(onDisposed)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/localchangemetadata-interface#getrevertible-methodsignature) | `Alpha` | [RevertibleAlpha](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/revertiblealpha-interface)| undefined | Returns an object (a ["revertible"](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/revertiblealpha-interface)) that can be used to revert the change that produced this event. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### isLocal[](https://fluidframework.com#islocal-propertysignature)

Whether the change was made on the local machine/client or received from a remote client.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#islocal-signature)

```
readonly isLocal: true;
```
**Type**: true

### label[](https://fluidframework.com#label-propertysignature)

Optional label provided by the user when commit was created. This can be used by undo/redo to group or classify edits.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#label-signature)

```
readonly label?: unknown;
```
**Type**: unknown

### labels[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-propertysignature)

A set of [labels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/runtransactionparams-interface#label-propertysignature) for all transactions (nested or otherwise) that made up this change. This can be used to identify, group, or filter changes — for example, to decide whether a change should be included in an undo/redo stack.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-signature)

```
readonly labels: TransactionLabels;
```
**Type**: [TransactionLabels](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/transactionlabels-typealias)

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-remarks)

The optional *tree* property provides the structural nesting of the transactions as a [LabelTree](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/labeltree-interface).

The `tree` property is present whenever the change was produced by a transaction that includes at least one label. If the change was unlabeled, `tree` is `undefined` and the set is empty.

#### Usage[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-examples)

##### Example 1[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-example1)

Checking whether a change was produced by a specific kind of transaction:

```
branch.events.on("changed", (metadata) => {
  if (metadata.labels.has("testLabel")) {
    // This change came from a transaction labeled "testLabel"
  }
});
```
##### Example 2[](https://fluidframework.com#labels-example2)

A nested transaction produces a tree that reflects the nesting:

```
tree.runTransaction(() => {
  tree.runTransaction(() => { ... }, { label: "inner" });
}, { label: "outer" });
// metadata.labels.has("inner") === true
// metadata.labels.tree will be:
//   { label: "outer", sublabels: [{ label: "inner", sublabels: [] }] }
```
## Method Details[](https://fluidframework.com#method-details)

### getChange[](https://fluidframework.com#getchange-methodsignature)

Returns a serializable object that encodes the change.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getchange-signature)

```
getChange(): JsonCompatibleReadOnly;
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#getchange-remarks)

This is only available for local changes. This change object can be [applied to another branch](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treebranchalpha-interface#applychange-methodsignature) in the same state as the one which generated it. The change object must be applied to a SharedTree with the same IdCompressor session ID as it was created from.

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getchange-returns)

**Return type**: [JsonCompatibleReadOnly](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/jsoncompatiblereadonly-typealias)

### getRevertible[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-methodsignature)

Returns an object (a ["revertible"](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/revertiblealpha-interface)) that can be used to revert the change that produced this event.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-signature)

```
getRevertible(onDisposed?: (revertible: RevertibleAlpha) => void): RevertibleAlpha | undefined;
```
#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-remarks)

This is only available for local changes. If the change is not revertible (for example, it was a change to the application schema), then this will return `undefined`. Revertibles should be disposed when they are no longer needed.

#### Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-parameters)

| Parameter | Modifiers | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| onDisposed | optional | (revertible: [RevertibleAlpha](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/revertiblealpha-interface)) => void | A callback that will be invoked when the `Revertible`is disposed. This happens when the`Revertible`is disposed manually or when the`TreeView`that the`Revertible`belongs to is disposed - whichever happens first. This is typically used to clean up any resources associated with the`Revertible`in the host application. |

#### Returns[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-returns)

**Return type**: [RevertibleAlpha](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/revertiblealpha-interface) | undefined

#### Error Handling[](https://fluidframework.com#getrevertible-throws)

Throws an error if called outside the scope of the `changed` event that provided it.

---

# MakeNominal Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/makenominal-interface

Use this as the type of a protected field to cause a type to use nominal typing instead of structural.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#makenominal-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface MakeNominal
```
## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#makenominal-remarks)

Using nominal typing in this way prevents assignment of objects which are not instances of this class to values of this class's type. Classes which are used with "instanceof", or are supposed to be instantiated in particular ways (not just made with object literals) can use this to prevent undesired assignments.

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#makenominal-example)

```
protected _typeCheck!: MakeNominal;
```

---

# MapNodeCustomizableSchemaUnsafe Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/mapnodecustomizableschemaunsafe-interface

[Unenforced](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/unenforced-typealias) version of [MapNodeCustomizableSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/mapnodecustomizableschema-interface)s.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#mapnodecustomizableschemaunsafe-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export interface MapNodeCustomizableSchemaUnsafe<out TName extends string, in out T extends System_Unsafe.ImplicitAllowedTypesUnsafe, out TCustomMetadata> extends TreeNodeSchemaClass<TName, NodeKind.Map, System_Unsafe.TreeMapNodeUnsafe<T> & WithType<TName, NodeKind.Map, T>, {
    [Symbol.iterator](): Iterator<[
        string,
        System_Unsafe.InsertableTreeNodeFromImplicitAllowedTypesUnsafe<T>
    ]>;
} | {
    readonly [P in string]: System_Unsafe.InsertableTreeNodeFromImplicitAllowedTypesUnsafe<T>;
}, false, T, undefined, TCustomMetadata>, SimpleMapNodeSchema<SchemaType.View, TCustomMetadata>
```

# NoChangeConstraint Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nochangeconstraint-interface

A [constraint](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/transactionconstraintalpha-typealias) which requires that, for this transaction to apply, the document must be in the same state immediately before the transaction is applied as it was before the transaction was authored. When used as a revert precondition it requires that, for the revert to apply, the document must be in the same state immediately before the revert is applied as it was after the transaction was applied.

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### changedProperties[](https://fluidframework.com#changedproperties-propertysignature)

When the node changed is an object or Map node, this lists all the properties which changed.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#changedproperties-signature)

```
readonly changedProperties?: ReadonlySet<TNode extends WithType<string, NodeKind.Object, infer TInfo> ? string & keyof TInfo : string>;
```
**Type**: ReadonlySet<TNode extends [WithType](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/withtype-interface)<string, [NodeKind.Object](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodekind-enum#object-enummember), infer TInfo> ? string & keyof TInfo : string>

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#changedproperties-remarks)

This only includes changes to the node itself (which would trigger [nodeChanged(unstable)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treechangeevents-interface#nodechanged-methodsignature)).

Not present when the [NodeKind](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodekind-enum) does not support this feature (currently just ArrayNodes).

When defined, the set should never be empty, since `nodeChanged` will only be triggered when there is a change, and for the supported node types, the only things that can change are properties.

# NodeProvider TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodeprovider-typealias

A provider for values in tree nodes.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#nodeprovider-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export type NodeProvider<T> = T | (() => T);
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Description |
|---|---|
| T |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#nodeprovider-remarks)

This type represents two ways to provide node values:

- **A value**: Provide any value directly (number, string, object, array, etc.). When a value is provided, the data is copied for each use to ensure independence between instances. The value must be of an allowed type for the field.

- **A generator function**: A function that returns a value. The function is called each time a default is needed, allowing for dynamic defaults or explicit control over value creation. The return value must be of an allowed type for the field.

Values should be preferred over generator functions when possible, as they are simpler and more efficient. Generator functions should be used when the default value needs to be dynamic or when it is not possible to provide a value directly.

## Example[](https://fluidframework.com#nodeprovider-example)

```
// Provide a value directly
factory.withDefault(factory.required(factory.string), "default")
factory.withDefault(factory.optional(Person), new Person({ name: "Guest" }))
// Use a generator function
factory.withDefault(factory.required(factory.string), () => crypto.randomUUID())
factory.withDefault(factory.optional(Person), () => new Person({ name: "Guest" }))
```

---
