#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#description-remarks)

If provided, will be used by the system in scenarios where a description of the kind of node is useful. E.g., when converting a Node Schema to [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org/), this description will be used as the `description` property.

---

# NumberKeys TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/numberkeys-typealias

Extracts the keys of `T` which are numbers.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#numberkeys-signature)

```
export type NumberKeys<T, Transformed = {
    readonly [Property in keyof T as number extends Property ? never : Property]: Property;
}> = Transformed[`${number}` & keyof Transformed];
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | ||
| Transformed | { readonly [Property in keyof T as number extends Property ? never : Property]: Property; } |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#numberkeys-remarks)

The keys are extracted as strings which can be used to index `T`.

This handles cases like `{ x: 4 } & [5, 6]` returning `"0"` and `"1"`. Such cases are difficult to handle since `keyof` includes `number` in such cases, but the type can not be indexed by `number`.

---

# ObjectFromSchemaRecord TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectfromschemarecord-typealias

Generates the properties for an ObjectNode from its field schema object.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#objectfromschemarecord-signature)

```
export type ObjectFromSchemaRecord<T extends RestrictiveStringRecord<ImplicitFieldSchema>> = RestrictiveStringRecord<ImplicitFieldSchema> extends T ? {} : {
    -readonly [Property in keyof T]: Property extends string ? TreeFieldFromImplicitField<T[Property]> : unknown;
};
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Description |
|---|---|---|
| T | [RestrictiveStringRecord](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/restrictivestringrecord-typealias)<[ImplicitFieldSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/implicitfieldschema-typealias)> |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#objectfromschemarecord-remarks)

Due to [https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/43826](https://github.com/microsoft/TypeScript/issues/43826), we can't enable implicit construction of [TreeNodes](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class) for setters. Therefore code assigning to these fields must explicitly construct nodes using the schema's constructor or create method, or using some other method like [create(schema, data)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#create-methodsignature).

---

# ObjectNodeSchemaWorkaround TypeAlias | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectnodeschemaworkaround-typealias

[ObjectNodeSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectnodeschema-interface) with a workaround to avoid a specific known TypeScript issue which causes it to not be assignable to itself in some cases.

This type is "sealed," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not implement or extend it. Future versions of this type may add members or make typing of readonly members more specific.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#objectnodeschemaworkaround-signature)

```
/** @sealed */
export type ObjectNodeSchemaWorkaround<TName extends string = string, T extends RestrictiveStringRecord<ImplicitFieldSchema> = RestrictiveStringRecord<ImplicitFieldSchema>, ImplicitlyConstructable extends boolean = boolean, TCustomMetadata = unknown> = ObjectNodeSchema<TName, T, ImplicitlyConstructable, TCustomMetadata> & {
    readonly createFromInsertable: unknown;
};
```
### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Constraint | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| TName | string | string | |
| T | [RestrictiveStringRecord](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/restrictivestringrecord-typealias)<[ImplicitFieldSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/implicitfieldschema-typealias)> | [RestrictiveStringRecord](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/restrictivestringrecord-typealias)<[ImplicitFieldSchema](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/implicitfieldschema-typealias)> | |
| ImplicitlyConstructable | boolean | boolean | |
| TCustomMetadata | unknown |

## Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#objectnodeschemaworkaround-remarks)

If dealing with a schema whose inferred type includes this workaround (because it was produced by a schema factory API which uses it), if you need to explicitly state that type (for example when using [isolatedDeclarations](https://www.typescriptlang.org/tsconfig/#isolatedDeclarations)), it is best to keep this workaround. No other case should need to refer to this workaround type directly. See *ObjectNodeSchemaWorkaround.createFromInsertable* for details.

---

# ObjectSchemaOptions Interface | Fluid Framework

Source: https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface

Options when declaring an [object node](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/schemafactory-class#object-method)'s schema.

This type is "input," meaning that code outside of the library defining it should not read from it. Future versions of this type may add optional members or make typing of members more general.

## Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#objectschemaoptions-signature)

```
export interface ObjectSchemaOptions<TCustomMetadata = unknown> extends NodeSchemaOptions<TCustomMetadata>
```
**Extends**: [NodeSchemaOptions](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/nodeschemaoptions-interface)<TCustomMetadata>

### Type Parameters[](https://fluidframework.com#type-parameters)

| Parameter | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| TCustomMetadata | unknown |

## Properties[](https://fluidframework.com#properties)

| Property | Alerts | Modifiers | Default Value | Type | Description |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [allowUnknownOptionalFields](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/objectschemaoptions-interface#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature) | `Beta` | `optional`,`readonly` | `false` | boolean | Allow nodes typed with this object node schema to contain optional fields that are not present in the schema declaration. Such nodes can come into existence either via import APIs (see remarks) or by way of collaboration with another client that has upgraded the document's schema to include those optional fields. |

## Property Details[](https://fluidframework.com#property-details)

### allowUnknownOptionalFields[](https://fluidframework.com#allowunknownoptionalfields-propertysignature)

Allow nodes typed with this object node schema to contain optional fields that are not present in the schema declaration. Such nodes can come into existence either via import APIs (see remarks) or by way of collaboration with another client that has upgraded the document's schema to include those optional fields.

#### Signature[](https://fluidframework.com#allowunknownoptionalfields-signature)

```
readonly allowUnknownOptionalFields?: boolean;
```
**Type**: boolean

#### Remarks[](https://fluidframework.com#allowunknownoptionalfields-remarks)

The advantage of enabling this option is that it allows an application ecosystem with staged rollout to more quickly upgrade documents to include schema for new optional features.

However, it does come with trade-offs that applications should weigh carefully when it comes to interactions between code and documents. When opening such documents, the API presented is still determined by the view schema. This can have implications on the behavior of edits or code which uses portions of the view schema, since this may inadvertently drop data which is present in those optional fields in the document schema.

Consider the following example:

```
const sf = new SchemaFactory("com.example");
class PersonView extends sf.object("Person", { name: sf.string }, { allowUnknownOptionalFields: true }) {}
class PersonStored extends sf.object("Person", { name: sf.string, nickname: sf.optional(sf.string) }) {}
// Say we have a document which uses `PersonStored` in its schema, and application code constructs
// a tree view using `PersonView`. If the application for some reason had implemented a function like this:
function clonePerson(a: PersonView): PersonView {
	return new PersonView({ name: a.name });
}
// ...or even like this:
function clonePerson(a: PersonView): PersonView {
 return new PersonView({ ...a})
}
// Then the alleged clone wouldn't actually clone the entire person in either case, it would drop the nickname.
```
The existing import and export APIs have similar problems. For example currently the [exportVerbose](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#exportverbose-methodsignature) API with stored keys preserves unknown optional fields, but [Unhydrated](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/unhydrated-typealias) nodes produced by [TreeNode](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treenode-class) constructors, insertable content, and [importVerbose](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treealpha-interface#importverbose-methodsignature) do not. [clone(node)](https://fluidframework.com/docs/api/fluid-framework/treebeta-interface#clone-methodsignature) however can be used to clone a node preserving unknown optional fields.

Note that public API methods which operate on entire nodes (such as `moveTo`, `moveToEnd`, etc. on arrays) do not encounter this problem as SharedTree's implementation stores the entire node in its lower layers. It's only when application code reaches into a node (either by accessing its fields, spreading it, or some other means) that this problem arises.

---
